definition_zh: 易弯的；柔韧的；易受影响的；顺从的
definition_en: easy to bend or shape, and by extension easy to influence or persuade
core_image: 柳条在手里弯成弧线，松手又能弹回
scene: 编筐的年轻人把一根柔软的新柳条弯成圆圈，因为它温热而又柔韧。The young basket maker bent the fresh willow into a ring because it was warm and pliable.
sceneCN: 这里 pliable 是「易弯的、柔韧的」（第 1 个义项：材料容易弯曲而不折断）；句意：年轻的编筐人把新鲜柳条弯成圆环，因为它温热柔韧。

pos.zh: 易受影响的；易被说服的；顺从的

collocations.zh: 可塑性强的大脑；易受影响的心智
太易受影响，扛不住压力

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ity 构成，指「柔韧性；易受影响性」
同源形容词，意为「顺从的；易弯的」，常作 pliable 的替换词
同族名词，源自法语「弯曲」一词，指夹持工具钳子

senses.title: Easy to bend without breaking
senses.definition: so flexible that it can be bent or shaped again and again without cracking
senses.definitionCN: 弹性好到可以反复弯曲或塑形而不会开裂
senses.example: Warm leather is far more pliable than cold leather.
senses.exampleCN: 温热的皮革比冷的柔软得多。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bend, and the core image is a material that gives way instead of snapping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本意是「弯曲」，核心意象是顺势弯下而不折断的材料。

senses.title: Hard, sharp, or stubborn
senses.titleCN: 僵硬的；执拗的（否定对照）
senses.definition: described as the opposite of what is rigid, brittle, or unwilling to change
senses.definitionCN: 作为「僵硬、易碎、不肯变通」的反面来描述人和事物
senses.example: Her argument was pliable in the face of new figures.
senses.exampleCN: 面对新数据，她的论点可以随时调整。
senses.why: Because the word stresses yielding, it is often used to contrast with rigid habits or stubborn views.
senses.whyCN: 由于它强调「让步」，常被用来与僵化的习惯或固执的看法形成对照。

senses.title: Easy to influence or persuade
senses.titleCN: 易受影响的；易被说服的
senses.definition: ready to accept advice or orders and quick to adapt to other people
senses.definitionCN: 乐于接受建议或指令、很快顺应他人的
senses.example: A good trainee is pliable but still asks questions.
senses.exampleCN: 好的学员乐于听指导，但仍会提问题。
senses.why: The physical bend becomes a mental bend: a person who can be shaped like clay by teachers or leaders.
senses.whyCN: 身体的「弯」变成心智的「弯」：像黏土一样被老师或领导塑造的人。

senses.title: Adaptable to changing conditions
senses.titleCN: 灵活可调的；有适应性的
senses.definition: able to be changed or adjusted easily when circumstances change
senses.definitionCN: 情况变化时容易改动或调整的
senses.example: The scheme is pliable enough to suit small towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案弹性足够大，也适合小城镇。
senses.why: Once the word covers people, it easily covers plans and rules that can be reshaped without damage.
senses.whyCN: 一旦该词可用于人，也就自然可以形容能被重塑而无损的方案与规则。

intro.en: Pliable comes from French plier, to bend, from Latin plicare, to fold, and the suffix -able, able to be.
intro.cn: pliable 来自法语 plier（弯曲），源于拉丁语 plicare（折叠），再加后缀 -able（能被……的）。

items.en: Plicare means to fold, to bend, or to lay together.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠、弯曲或把东西叠在一起。

items.en: Plier develops the sense of bending or yielding.
items.cn: plier 发展出弯曲、屈服的意思。

items.en: Pliable forms in French as able to be bent.
items.cn: 法语中形成 pliable，表示「能被弯曲的」。

items.en: Middle English borrows pliable for things that bend easily.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 pliable，指容易弯曲的东西。

items.en: The word extends from materials to minds and manners.
items.cn: 该词从材料进一步扩展到心智和举止。

items.en: Technical and design writing keeps the material sense alive.
items.cn: 技术与设计写作让它的材料义持续存活。

note.en: Pliable sits in a large folding family, from ply to apply, and is close to flexible and supple.
note.cn: pliable 属于庞大的「折叠」词族，从 ply 到 apply，与 flexible、supple 意义接近。

entries.definition: easily bent or yielding
entries.definitionCN: 柔顺的；易弯的（与 pliable 同出 plicare）

entries.definition: a hand tool with jaws for gripping
entries.definitionCN: 钳子；老虎钳（同出法语「弯曲」一词，只是用法不同）

entries.definition: to put something onto or into use
entries.definitionCN: 应用；贴附（同出拉丁语「折叠、贴合」词根）

entries.definition: able to bend without breaking
entries.definitionCN: 柔韧的；灵活的（最通用的对应词）

entries.definition: bending and moving easily
entries.definitionCN: 柔软灵活的（多形容身体或皮革）

entries.definition: able to be pulled into a wire
entries.definitionCN: 有延展性的；可拉成丝的（金属专用术语）

normalIntro.en: Pliable says that a thing can be bent: fold it, and it gives way instead of breaking.
normalIntro.cn: pliable 说的是「能被弯」：折它一下，它会顺着弯，而不是折断。

normal.en: The -able ending is the key: pliable means able to be plied, that is, bent.
normal.cn: 结尾是关键：pliable 意为「能被弯的」，即 able to be plied。

normal.en: The same folding root appears in apply, comply, and reply.
normal.cn: 同一个「折叠」词根还出现在 apply、comply、reply 里。

normal.en: Pliability is the noun, and pliant is the shorter twin adjective.
normal.cn: 名词是 pliability，较短的同源形容词是 pliant。

normal.en: For people, pliable often carries a warning of being too easily led.
normal.cn: 形容人时，pliable 常暗含「太容易被牵着走」的提醒。

normal.en: Contrast pliable with brittle: one bends, the other snaps.
normal.cn: 对比 brittle：一个会弯，一个会断。

abstract.en: Hold a willow wand and bend it into a circle.
abstract.cn: 手里拿一根柳条，把它弯成一个圆。

abstract.en: Watch a stiff board splinter while a thin sheet of tin curls.
abstract.cn: 看硬木板裂成渣，而一片薄锡却卷了起来。

abstract.en: Picture clay taking any thumbprint without a crack.
abstract.cn: 想象黏土随着指印变形，却从不裂开。

examples.en: Rubber is pliable, so it seals the joint when the pipe moves.
examples.cn: 橡胶富有弹性，所以在管道晃动时仍能密封接口。

examples.en: Years of teaching had left him pliable rather than stubborn.
examples.cn: 多年教学让他变得随和，而不是固执。

examples.en: The rules are pliable enough to fit a small school.
examples.cn: 这些规则的弹性足够适应一所小学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不来硬的」——一弯就顺，不来硬的，正是柔韧；这只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 plicare（折叠、弯曲）→ 法语 plier（弯曲）→ 法语 pliable → 英语 pliable，核心义「能被弯而不坏」，引申为「易受影响、灵活」。

sensesIntro.en: Pliable begins with materials that bend, contrasts with brittle and rigid things, then widens to people who are easily guided and to plans that can adapt.
sensesIntro.cn: pliable 从可弯曲的材料说起，与易碎、僵硬之物相对，再扩展到容易听人摆布的人以及可灵活调整的方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of willow bowed into an arc by hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根柳条被手弯成弧线。

branches.en: Flexible material is the earliest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 柔韧的材料是出现最早、最字面的义项。

branches.en: The word is felt as the opposite of hard or brittle things.
branches.cn: 它被当作坚硬或易碎之物的反面来感受。

branches.en: A pliable person is clay in someone else hands.
branches.cn: 易受影响的人就像别人手里的黏土。

branches.en: Adapting a plan and adapting oneself both reuse the bending image.
branches.cn: 调整方案与顺应他人都在复用「弯曲」的意象。

branches.en: The contrast with brittle defines the material sense from the outside.
branches.cn: 与易碎的对立从反面划定了材料义的边界。

intro.en: Pliable is built from the folding root plic- plus -able, and it shares its family with apply, comply, and supple.
intro.cn: pliable 由「折叠」词根 plic- 加 -able 构成，与 apply、comply 以及 supple 属同一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare means to fold, and its forms spread into French, English, and many everyday verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，其各种形式扩散到法语、英语以及许多日常动词中。

items.example: The root plic- supplies the bending idea.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供了「弯曲」的核心概念。

items.example: The suffix -able turns bend able into bendable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把词根变成「能被弯曲的」。

items.example: The French verb plier means to bend.
items.exampleCN: 法语动词 plier 意为弯曲。

items.example: Ply a trade literally means working at it.
items.exampleCN: ply a trade 字面上就是从事一门手艺。

items.meaning: to put on or put to use
items.example: Apply builds on the fold of a sheet.
items.exampleCN: apply 建立在「折叠、贴合」的意象上。

items.example: To comply is to fold oneself to the rule.
items.exampleCN: comply 就是「把自己折向」规则。

items.example: Supple shares the same soft bending sense.
items.exampleCN: supple 同样表示柔软的弯曲。

items.example: Pliant is the shorter sibling of pliable.
items.exampleCN: pliant 是 pliable 的简短兄弟词。

items.example: Pliability names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: pliability 指这种「柔韧」性质本身。

items.meaning: to make something folded or tangled
items.example: Complicate folds things together into a tangle.
items.exampleCN: complicate 把事物折叠、缠在一起。

definition_zh: 困境；苦境；保证；宣誓
definition_en: a difficult and unhappy situation, or old use a solemn promise
core_image: 旅人站在断桥边，前后都是湍急的河水
scene: 洪水冲走了唯一的小桥，两个老人被困在河对岸的小屋里。The villagers described the plight of the two old men whose bridge had washed away.
sceneCN: 这里 plight 是「困境、苦境」（第 1 个义项：令人痛苦而难以摆脱的处境）；句意：村民们讲述那两位老人因桥被冲走而陷入的困境。

pos.zh: 保证；誓约（古旧或法律用语）

collocations.phrase: draw attention to the plight of
collocations.zh: 引起人们对……困境的关注

collocations.phrase: highlight the plight of the homeless
collocations.zh: 凸显无家可归者的困境

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，常见于旧式短语「plighted troth」，意为「已订婚的；已许诺的」
旧式动词用法，意为「以誓约担保；许诺」，现代英语极少使用
同义替换词，指「尴尬而棘手的困境」，常与 plight 对照使用

senses.title: A difficult and unhappy situation
senses.definition: a serious and unhappy condition in which someone has little power to escape
senses.definitionCN: 某人几乎无力摆脱的严重而痛苦的处境
senses.example: The report describes the plight of factory workers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描述了工厂工人的困境。
senses.why: The modern noun names a dangerous circumstance, and it usually belongs to people the speaker pities.
senses.whyCN: 现代名词指危险的处境，且通常属于说话人同情的人。

senses.title: A solemn promise
senses.definition: an old and formal word for a promise made before witnesses
senses.definitionCN: 在证人面前作出的承诺，属古旧而正式的说法
senses.example: They exchanged plights of faith before the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在众人面前互立信诺。
senses.why: An older verb meaning to pledge gave the noun the sense of a binding word.
senses.whyCN: 更早的动词「以保证为质」让名词获得了「有约束力的诺言」这一义。

senses.title: A risky or entangled state
senses.definition: a situation woven like a net, where each move draws the person deeper in
senses.definitionCN: 像网一样织起来的处境，每动一步都陷得更深
senses.example: Caught in the plight of debt, the family sold its shop.
senses.exampleCN: 陷入债务纠缠，这家人卖掉了店铺。
senses.why: The folding and weaving image behind the old senses colors the modern one: a plight is a situation one is wrapped up in.
senses.whyCN: 古义背后「折叠、编织」的意象为现代义着上了底色：plight 就是把人裹住的处境。

intro.en: Plight is uncertain in origin; an Old French noun plit or ploit meaning a folded condition has been proposed, but scholars do not agree.
intro.cn: plight 的词源来源不确定；有人认为来自古法语名词 plit 或 ploit（折叠的状态），但学界意见并不一致。

items.en: A noun of unclear form appears in legal and common speech.
items.cn: 一个词形尚不明确的名词在法语与法律用语中现身。

items.en: Some sources link the word to a noun for a folded state or condition.
items.cn: 部分资料把该词与表示「折叠状态」的名词联系起来，属推测。

items.en: Plight is recorded in the sense of a pledge or promise.
items.cn: 英语中的 plight 最早记作「保证、誓约」。

items.en: The sense of an unlucky or dangerous situation becomes common.
items.cn: 「不幸或危险的处境」这一义变得常见。

items.en: Today the situation sense dominates, and the promise sense is archaic.
items.cn: 今天以「处境」义为主，「誓约」义已成古语。

note.en: Plight is almost alone in its spelling; the closest neighbours are pledge and plight words for trouble.
note.cn: plight 在拼写上几乎没有亲族；最接近的邻居是 pledge 以及表示「麻烦、困境」的一类词。

entries.definition: a serious promise or a thing given as security
entries.definitionCN: 誓言；抵押物（与 plight 的「誓约」义相近，但拼写与词源都不同）

entries.definition: the act of flying or running away
entries.definitionCN: 飞行；逃跑（只是拼写与读音相近，词源来自「飞」）

entries.definition: small in amount, or to insult someone lightly
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的；轻视（只是拼写相近，词源来自「平滑」）

entries.definition: an awkward and difficult situation
entries.definitionCN: 困境；窘境

entries.definition: suffering caused by difficult conditions
entries.definitionCN: 艰难；困苦（强调承受的苦，不着重「处境」全景）

entries.definition: great unhappiness or suffering
entries.definitionCN: 痛苦；悲惨（偏情绪与感受）

normalIntro.en: Plight keeps two lives: an old promise and a modern hard situation, and both come from the idea of being bound.
normalIntro.cn: plight 有两种生命：古老诺言与现代苦境，两者都源于「被缚住」的感觉。

normal.en: The most common frame is the plight of plus a group, as in the plight of refugees.
normal.cn: 最常见的框架是「the plight of」加某个群体，例如难民的困境。

normal.en: Plight always carries sympathy; a neutral trouble is simply a difficulty.
normal.cn: plight 总带同情；中性的麻烦只叫 difficulty。

normal.en: The old verb gives the phrase plighted troth, a promise of marriage.
normal.cn: 旧式动词留下短语 plighted troth，即婚约。

normal.en: Its spelling is one of a kind: keep the p, keep the silent-like gh, and drop the extra letters other words have.
normal.cn: 它的拼写独一份：记住开头的 p，记住轻声的 gh，别加多余字母。

normal.en: Compare pledge: pledge is the promise itself, while plight now most often means the trouble one is in.
normal.cn: 对比 pledge：pledge 是诺言本身，而 plight 现在多指人陷入的困境。

abstract.en: See a traveller on a broken bridge, water fast on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一位旅人站在断桥边，两侧都是湍急的水。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to promise in front of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在众人面前举起起誓的手。

abstract.en: Imagine a net pulling tighter each time someone moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网，每动一下就收得更紧。

examples.en: The film made the plight of farmers visible to a wide audience.
examples.cn: 这部影片让广大观众看见了农民的困境。

examples.en: After the storm, the village presented a sorry plight.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，村子景象一片狼狈。

examples.en: The old poem speaks of plighted love, not of danger.
examples.cn: 那首古诗说的是立约的爱情，而并非危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来特」——麻烦「扑来」得特别凶，就是困境；这只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 词源来源不确定；一般认为与古法语中表示「折叠、纠缠状态」的名词有关（推测），另有来自保证义词的影子，现代核心义「被困住的处境」。

sensesIntro.en: Plight moves from a binding promise to a dangerous situation, and finally to a tangled state people cannot escape.
sensesIntro.cn: plight 从有约束力的诺言转向危险的处境，最后指人无法脱身的纠缠状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller facing a broken bridge with swift water below.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人面对断桥，桥下是湍急的河水。

branches.en: A hard and unhappy situation is the everyday sense today.
branches.cn: 艰难而不幸的处境是今天最日常的义项。

branches.en: The promise sense survives in formal and archaic writing.
branches.cn: 誓约义残存在正式与古旧的文字里。

branches.en: A tangled state is the image of being wrapped up in trouble.
branches.cn: 纠缠状态就是被麻烦裹住的图景。

branches.en: A plight is a situation that surrounds a person like a net.
branches.cn: plight 是一种像网一样把人围住的处境。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of being bound.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「被缚住」的观念。

intro.en: Plight has almost no affix family of its own, so its word web is built from pledge, flight, and slight.
intro.cn: plight 几乎没有自己的词缀家族，它的词网要靠 pledge、flight、slight 等词来搭建。

latinIntro.en: It is uncertain whether Latin contributed a form; compare the Latin root for folding, plicare, with caution.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语是否贡献了词形并不确定；可谨慎地对照表示「折叠」的拉丁词根 plicare。

items.example: Plight is a noun only, never a verb in modern use.
items.exampleCN: 现代英语中 plight 只作名词，不作动词。

items.example: The plural plights appears mostly in formal texts.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式多出现在正式文本中。

items.example: Plighted troth is an old phrase for an engagement.
items.exampleCN: plighted troth 是「婚约」的旧式说法。

items.example: Pledge is a near neighbour in sound and sense.
items.exampleCN: pledge 在读音与意义上都是近邻。

items.example: Flight differs only in its first two letters.
items.exampleCN: flight 只是头两个字母不同。

items.example: Slight sounds like plight but has a different root.
items.exampleCN: slight 听起来像 plight，但词根不同。

items.example: Bright joins the family of -ight spellings.
items.exampleCN: bright 也属于 -ight 拼写的一组词。

items.example: Delight belongs to the same -ight pattern.
items.exampleCN: delight 属于同一 -ight 拼写模式。

items.example: Troth pairs with plighted in old marriage vows.
items.exampleCN: troth 与 plighted 在旧式婚誓中搭配使用。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 折叠（仅作推测性对照，并非已证来源）

definition_zh: 犁；耕犁（农具）；犁地；翻耕；艰难前行； plough into 猛撞； plough back 再投资； plough through 费力读完
definition_en: a farm tool with a heavy blade that turns over soil, or to turn over soil with it, or to move forward with effort
core_image: 一块沉重的铁犁刀切开泥土，把土翻成一道整齐的长沟
scene: 春耕时节，老农赶着牛在田里来回走。Every spring the farmer yokes the ox and ploughs the old field before sowing seed.
sceneCN: 这里 plough 是动词「犁地、翻耕」（第 2 个义项：用犁把土翻起来）；句意：每年春天，农夫给牛套上轭，播种前先犁老田。

pos.zh: 犁地；翻耕；艰难前行；猛撞；再投资

derivatives.zh: 由 plough 加 man 构成，指扶犁耕地的人
由 plough 加 share（切割部分）构成，指犁铧，即犁上切开土壤的铁刀
由 plough 加 -ing 构成动名词，指犁地这一农事活动
由 plough 加 land 构成，指可耕地；历史上也指牛队一天能耕完的面积

senses.title: A heavy farm tool that turns soil
senses.definition: a large farming tool with a heavy blade pulled by an animal or machine to turn up the soil
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型农具，带有沉重的刀片，由牲畜或机器牵引来翻起土壤
senses.example: The old plough stood rusting in the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 那架旧犁摆在棚屋里生锈。
senses.why: Old English ploh named the exact object first, a board or blade that cuts and lifts earth, before any extended meaning grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ploh 最早命名的就是这件实物，一块切开并翻起泥土的板或刀，其他引申义都从这件实物长出来。

senses.title: To turn over soil with a plough
senses.definition: to break up and turn over soil with a plough, usually before planting crops
senses.definitionCN: 用犁翻起土壤，通常是在播种庄稼之前
senses.example: Farmers plough the land in late autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在深秋犁地。
senses.why: The verb is simply the tool put into action, so the concrete object turns directly into the act of lifting and folding soil.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把农具拿来使用，这个具体物件直接转化成「翻起并折过泥土」的动作。

senses.title: To move forward with difficulty
senses.definition: to move forward slowly and with effort, especially through something heavy or deep
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而费力地向前移动，尤指穿过沉重或很深的东西
senses.example: The truck ploughed through the deep mud.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车艰难地穿过深深的泥浆。
senses.why: A plough has to be forced through hard ground, so the image of pushing something heavy forward gives the sense of laboured movement.
senses.whyCN: 犁必须被硬推过坚硬的土，于是「把沉重之物往前推」的画面就延伸出费力的移动。

senses.title: A machine for clearing snow
senses.definition: a machine or vehicle attachment with a wide blade that pushes snow or debris off a road
senses.definitionCN: 带宽大刀片的机器或车辆附件，把雪或杂物从道路上推开
senses.example: A snow plough cleared the road by dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，一辆扫雪机就把路清出来了。
senses.why: The wide blade that pushes a furrow through soil became a wide blade that pushes a furrow through snow, keeping the same shape but changing the material.
senses.whyCN: 在土里推出沟的宽刀片，变成了在雪里推出沟的宽刀片，形状没变，只是被推的材料换了。

senses.title: To crash into something
senses.definition: to hit or crash into something with great force, usually while moving fast
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的力量撞上某物，通常发生在快速移动时
senses.example: The bus skidded and ploughed into the barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车打滑后猛地撞上了护栏。
senses.why: The plough image of driving a heavy blade straight into something gives us the violent forward impact of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 犁头直直插进土里的画面，提供了这一义项中「沉重之物径直撞上去」的暴力感。

senses.title: To put money back into a business
senses.definition: to invest money earned from a business back into the same business
senses.definitionCN: 把企业赚到的钱再投回同一家企业
senses.example: The company ploughs its profits back into research.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把利润再投入研究。
senses.why: Money turned back into the land instead of being taken out mirrors seed being planted for a later crop, so reinvestment borrows the farming picture.
senses.whyCN: 钱不取走而是重新回到土地里，就像种子种下等待下一季收成，所以再投资借用了耕作的画面。

senses.title: To work steadily through something
senses.definition: to work through a long or difficult task, text, or amount of work steadily and with effort
senses.definitionCN: 持续而费力地做完一段漫长或困难的任务、文本或大量工作
senses.example: She ploughed through three hours of paperwork.
senses.exampleCN: 她埋头处理了三个小时的文件。
senses.why: Going through a field slowly, row after row, gives the picture of pushing steadily through a long stretch of hard material.
senses.whyCN: 一块田一块田地慢慢走完，就形成了「在一长段坚硬材料中持续推进」的画面。

senses.title: The Plough as a group of stars
senses.definition: a group of seven stars in the constellation Ursa Major, named for the shape of the tool
senses.definitionCN: 大熊星座中的七颗星，因其形状像犁而得名
senses.example: At night the Plough hangs above the northern sky.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，北斗七星挂在北方天空。
senses.why: The stars of the constellation outline the blade and the long handle, so the tool name was applied to the shape seen in the sky.
senses.whyCN: 这组星座的星点勾画出犁铧与长柄的轮廓，于是这件农具的名字被用来命名天上的形状。

intro.en: Plough goes back to Old English ploh, a word of Germanic origin that named the farming tool, and its American spelling plow follows the same word.
intro.cn: plough 源自日耳曼语系的古英语 ploh，最初就指这件农具；美式拼写 plow 是同一个词。

items.en: A Germanic form often reconstructed as plogaz is the probable ancestor, though the older roots behind it are uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为其祖先是原始日耳曼语的重构形式 plogaz，但它更早的词根来源尚不确定。

items.en: Ploh or plōh names the plough as an object, and also the land measure tied to the work of an ox team.
items.cn: 古英语 ploh 或 plōh 指犁这种物件，也指与牛队耕作量挂钩的土地单位。

items.en: Some scholars link the word to an old root for a flat board or slab, but this idea is rebuilt from later forms rather than proved.
items.cn: 有学者把它联系到意为「平板、厚板」的古老词根，但这一说法是从后世形式重构出来的，并未得到证实。

items.en: Spellings such as plough become the usual written form in later Middle English, and the verb grows beside the noun.
items.cn: plough 等拼法在中古英语后期成为通行写法，同时动词也在名词旁边长出来。

items.en: English carried the word to North America, where plow became the standard spelling in use.
items.cn: 英语把这个词带到北美，在那里 plow 成为通行的拼写。

items.en: New uses grow from the tool, such as snow plough, plough into traffic, and star names like the Plough.
items.cn: 现代英语从农具衍生出 snow plough、plough into traffic 以及指星群的 the Plough 等新用法。

note.en: Plough is close to its American spelling plow, the farm word family of ploughman, ploughshare and ploughland, and to other words about cutting, spreading and night skies.
note.cn: plough 与美式拼写 plow、ploughman 与 ploughshare 等农耕词族，以及表示切割、铺撒与夜空的词相邻。

entries.definition: the American spelling of plough, and the same word with the same history
entries.definitionCN: plough 的美式拼写，同一个词，来历也相同

entries.definition: a person who guides a plough
entries.definitionCN: 扶犁耕地的人

entries.definition: the iron cutting blade of a plough
entries.definitionCN: 犁铧；犁上切土的铁刀

entries.definition: to gather the crops from a field, the later step after ploughing
entries.definitionCN: 收割庄稼；犁地之后的下一步农事

entries.definition: to plant seeds in soil that has been prepared, often by ploughing
entries.definitionCN: 在准备好的（常是犁过的）地里播种

entries.definition: to prepare land for crops with a tool
entries.definitionCN: 耕作；用农具准备耕地

normalIntro.en: Plough is the iron blade that cuts the field, and every new meaning keeps the idea of a heavy blade pushed forward.
normalIntro.cn: plough 是切开土地的铁犁刀，它的每个新含义都保留着「沉重的刀片向前推」这一想法。

normal.en: Plough is the British spelling and plow is the American one; both are correct.
normal.cn: plough 是英式拼写，plow 是美式拼写，两者都对。

normal.en: A ploughman is the man behind the plough, and the ploughshare is its iron blade.
normal.cn: ploughman 是扶着犁的人，ploughshare 是犁上的铁刀。

normal.en: Plough into means to crash into, because a blade is driven straight in.
normal.cn: plough into 意为猛撞，因为刀片是直直插进去的。

normal.en: To plough through a long report is to work slowly and steadily through it.
normal.cn: plough through a long report 就是缓慢而稳当地把长报告做完。

normal.en: Compare sow and harvest: plough comes first, seeds next, crops last.
normal.cn: 对比 sow 和 harvest：先犁地，再播种，最后收割。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy blade folding a long ribbon of dark soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一块沉重的刀片把泥土翻成一条长长的深色带子。

abstract.en: Feel the slow push of a plough cutting a straight furrow through a field.
abstract.cn: 感受犁在田里慢慢推进、切出一条笔直犁沟的力道。

abstract.en: Think of a truck forcing its way through thick snow to reach a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车费劲地推开厚厚的雪，一路驶向村庄。

examples.en: The farmer uses a steel plough to break the hard ground.
examples.cn: 农夫用钢犁破开坚硬的土地。

examples.en: He ploughed through the mud for hours before reaching home.
examples.cn: 他在泥浆里艰难跋涉了几个小时才到家。

examples.en: The firm plans to plough its profits back into new equipment.
examples.cn: 这家公司打算把利润再投入新设备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼捞」——把挖出的土「泼」到一边、再「捞」起来翻个身，就是犁地；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自原始日耳曼语重构形式 plogaz，古英语作 ploh、plōh，本义「犁」；更早的词根来源不确定，美式拼写作 plow。

sensesIntro.en: Plough starts as the tool, then becomes the act of turning soil, and from that image grow laboured movement, the snow blade, the crash, reinvestment, hard work, and the star shape.
sensesIntro.cn: plough 先指农具，再指翻土的动作，之后从「沉重刀片向前推」这一画面生出艰难前行、推雪机、猛撞、再投资、埋头苦干，以及星群的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy iron blade cutting and folding soil into a furrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的铁刀切入土里，把土翻成犁沟。

branches.en: The concrete tool is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 具体的农具是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Turning soil with the tool is the action sense.
branches.cn: 用农具翻土是动作义项。

branches.en: Laboured movement and crashing both come from a blade forced forward.
branches.cn: 艰难前行与猛撞都来自「刀片被硬推向前」。

branches.en: The snow blade and hard work both keep the steady push along a line.
branches.cn: 推雪机与埋头苦干都保留了沿一条线持续推进。

branches.en: Reinvestment replants the harvest, and the stars take the outline of the tool.
branches.cn: 再投资把收成重新种回地里，星群则借用农具的轮廓。

intro.en: Plough is a native Germanic word, and its English family is built by compounding, with ploughman, ploughshare, ploughland and the -ing form ploughing.
intro.cn: plough 是本土的日耳曼语词，英语词族主要靠复合构词，如 ploughman、ploughshare、ploughland 以及加 -ing 的 ploughing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for plough, but Latin does supply near-meaning farming words such as aratrum and sulcus.
latinIntro.cn: plough 没有拉丁语来源，但拉丁语提供了 aratrum 与 sulcus 等意义相近的农耕词可供对照。

items.example: American English writes the word as plow.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语把这个词写作 plow。

items.meaning: a person who does the action
items.example: The suffix -man forms ploughman.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -man 构成 ploughman。

items.meaning: a person who works a plough
items.example: Ploughman joins the tool and its user.
items.exampleCN: ploughman 把农具与使用者结合在一起。

items.example: Share here names a cutting part, not a portion.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 share 指切割部件，而不是「份额」。

items.meaning: the iron blade of a plough
items.example: Ploughshare combines the tool with its blade.
items.exampleCN: ploughshare 把犁与它的刀片合在一起。

items.example: Ploughland adds land to the tool name.
items.exampleCN: ploughland 在农具名称后加上土地。

items.example: Ploughing names the farm activity.
items.exampleCN: ploughing 指犁地这项农事。

items.meaning: a machine that pushes snow off roads
items.example: Snow plough puts snow before the tool name.
items.exampleCN: snow plough 在农具名之前加上雪。

items.example: Plough into means to hit hard.
items.exampleCN: plough into 表示猛烈撞击。

items.meaning: the seven stars of Ursa Major
items.meaningCN: 北斗七星（大熊星座七颗星）
items.example: The tool name becomes a star name.
items.exampleCN: 农具名变成了星群名。

definition_zh: 长绒；毛绒织物；毛绒的；豪华的；奢华的
definition_en: a thick soft fabric with a long pile, or made of it, or luxurious and expensive in a showy way
core_image: 一张深红色的长绒沙发，手指按下去绒毛顺着一个方向倒
scene: 酒店大堂里摆着一排深红色的丝绒沙发。The lobby was furnished with deep velvet armchairs and a plush carpet underfoot.
sceneCN: 这里 plush 是形容词「毛绒的、厚软的」（第 3 个义项：像长绒织物那样厚软）；句意：大堂里摆着深红色天鹅绒扶手椅，脚下铺着厚软的长绒地毯。

pos.zh: 长绒的；柔软厚实的；奢华的；豪华的

derivatives.zh: 由 plush 加 -y 构成，指柔软蓬松的、厚实的
由 plush 加 -ness 构成名词，指柔软厚实或奢华的程度
由 plush 加 -ly 构成副词，指豪华舒适地

senses.title: A thick fabric with a long soft pile
senses.definition: a heavy fabric with a long soft pile on one side, used for upholstery and luxury clothing
senses.definitionCN: 一种厚重的织物，一侧有长长的柔软绒毛，用于家具装饰和华丽服装
senses.example: The seat covers were made of a rich red plush.
senses.exampleCN: 座椅套是用一种深红色的长绒布做的。
senses.why: The noun came straight from French pluche, a word for shaggy fabric, so the material was the word first meaning.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接来自法语 pluche（指长绒毛织物），所以「这种材料本身」就是这个词最早的意思。

senses.title: Short for plush fabric items
senses.definition: items or garments made from plush, or the plural form naming fabrics of that kind
senses.definitionCN: 用长绒织物制成的物件或衣服，复数形式用来指这一类织物
senses.example: In the shop window hung hats and plushes of many shades.
senses.exampleCN: 橱窗里挂着许多色调的帽子和丝绒料子。
senses.why: English often uses a material noun for the things made from it, so the fabric word also came to name plush goods.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用材料名词代指用它做成的东西，所以这个织物词也被用来指丝绒制品。

senses.title: Soft, thick and velvety
senses.definition: soft, thick and covered in a short velvety surface that is pleasant to touch
senses.definitionCN: 柔软厚实，表面覆盖着短而像天鹅绒一样舒服的毛
senses.example: The cat slept on a plush cushion.
senses.exampleCN: 猫睡在一个毛绒坐垫上。
senses.why: The descriptive adjective grew from the noun by keeping the one quality people notice first, the softness under the hand.
senses.whyCN: 描述性形容词由名词长出来，保留了人们最先注意到的特征：手摸上去非常柔软。

senses.title: Luxurious and expensively furnished
senses.definition: expensive, comfortable and aiming at luxury, often used of rooms, cars or services
senses.definitionCN: 昂贵、舒适且刻意奢华，常用于房间、汽车或服务
senses.example: They stayed at a plush hotel near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在车站附近一家豪华酒店。
senses.why: Only the rich could once afford plush, so the fabric name turned into a sign of wealth and comfort.
senses.whyCN: 过去只有富人用得起长绒织物，于是织物名变成了财富与舒适的标志。

senses.title: Too rich or showy
senses.definition: showing off comfort and wealth in a way that can seem excessive
senses.definitionCN: 炫耀舒适与富有，给人一种过分、甚至浮夸的感觉
senses.example: The plush decor of the club felt heavy to her.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部过分华丽的装饰让她觉得压抑。
senses.why: A word for luxury can slide into a word for excess, because the same soft surface almost hides the cost behind it.
senses.whyCN: 表示豪华的词容易滑向表示过度的词，因为同样柔软的表面几乎掩盖了背后的花费。

senses.title: Wealthy or well off
senses.definition: having plenty of money and comfortably living well, used of people or lifestyles
senses.definitionCN: 很有钱、生活舒适，指人或生活方式
senses.example: He grew up in a plush part of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里一个富裕的地段长大。
senses.why: Apply the luxury adjective to people and places, and the material word comes to stand for being comfortably rich.
senses.whyCN: 把这个豪华形容词用到人和地方上，织物词就转而表示「生活宽裕而富有」。

intro.en: Plush is borrowed from French pluche, a name for a shaggy or hairy fabric, which is related to the verb pelucher, to become fluffy.
intro.cn: plush 借自法语 pluche，指一种毛茸茸、有长毛的织物，与动词 pelucher（起绒、变蓬松）同源。

items.en: The probable base is Latin pilus, meaning a hair, which gives the hairy image behind the fabric.
items.cn: 一般认为基础是拉丁语 pilus（毛发），它提供了这种织物「长毛」的意象。

items.en: Peluche or peluche appears as a word for a shaggy textile, built on the idea of hair or wool.
items.cn: 古法语 peluche 出现，指长毛的纺织品，由毛发或羊毛的意象构成。

items.en: Modern French pluche is the form English took directly, naming a long-pile velvet-like cloth.
items.cn: 法语 pluche 是英语直接借用的形式，指一种长绒、类似天鹅绒的布。

items.en: Plush is first recorded in the sixteenth century as the name of the fabric itself.
items.cn: plush 在十六世纪首次见于记录，最初就是这种织物的名称。

items.en: The adjective sense of wealthy and luxurious spreads, especially in descriptions of hotels, drawing rooms and parlours.
items.cn: 「富有、奢华」的形容词含义逐渐流行，尤其用于形容酒店、客厅与接待室。

items.en: Plush now covers soft everyday comfort and luxury branding, from plush toys to plush offices.
items.cn: 现代英语中 plush 既指日常的柔软舒适，也用于奢华品牌语，从毛绒玩具到豪华办公室。

note.en: Plush is close to other names for soft pile fabrics such as velvet and velour, and to words for luxury living such as lavish and posh.
note.cn: plush 与 velvet、velour 等长绒织物名相邻，也与 lavish、posh 等表示奢华生活的词相邻。

entries.definition: soft and thick like plush
entries.definitionCN: 像长绒织物一样柔软厚实的

entries.definition: the quality of being soft, thick or luxurious
entries.definitionCN: 柔软厚实或奢华的特性

entries.definition: in a comfortable and luxurious way
entries.definitionCN: 奢华舒适地

entries.definition: a smooth heavy fabric with a short dense pile
entries.definitionCN: 光滑厚实、绒毛短而密的织物

entries.definition: a soft fabric with a pile like velvet
entries.definitionCN: 绒毛像天鹅绒一样的柔软织物

entries.definition: very generous or rich and costly in style
entries.definitionCN: 非常丰富阔绰、风格昂贵的

entries.definition: elegant and expensive in an informal British way
entries.definitionCN: 优雅昂贵的（英式口语）

normalIntro.en: Plush keeps one picture from French, a cloth covered in soft hair, and the fabric sense turns into both softness and luxury.
normalIntro.cn: plush 保留了法语的画面：一种长满柔软短毛的布；这个织物义再分成「柔软」与「奢华」两条路。

normal.en: Plush came from French pluche, and velour is its French cousin for a similar fabric.
normal.cn: plush 来自法语 pluche，velour 是它在法语里指类似织物的近亲。

normal.en: Plush describes a sofa or carpet by touch, while velvet usually names the cloth itself.
normal.cn: plush 多数用触感来形容沙发或地毯，而 velvet 通常直接指布料本身。

normal.en: Plusher and plushest follow the double consonant rule, like bigger and biggest.
normal.cn: plusher 与 plushest 遵循双写辅音规则，就像 bigger 与 biggest。

normal.en: Note the difference from flush and blush, which are spelled alike but have no connection to fabric.
normal.cn: 注意与 flush、blush 的区别，它们拼写相近，但与织物毫无关系。

normal.en: A plush toy is a soft stuffed toy, which is why the word now covers small soft comfort as well as luxury.
normal.cn: plush toy 是柔软的填充玩具，因此这个词既指小巧的柔软舒适，也指奢华。

abstract.en: Stroke a long-pile carpet with one hand to feel the single direction of the nap.
abstract.cn: 用手顺着摸一遍长绒地毯，感受绒毛只朝一个方向倒下的手感。

abstract.en: See a deep red velvet chair standing in the middle of a bright empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张深红丝绒椅子，孤零零站在明亮而空旷的房间里。

abstract.en: Think of a hotel lobby where every surface looks soft and none looks cheap.
abstract.cn: 想象一间酒店大堂，每一处表面都显得柔软，也都不显得廉价。

examples.en: The curtains were made of thick crimson plush.
examples.cn: 窗帘是用厚实的深红色长绒布做的。

examples.en: The children hugged their plush bears all night.
examples.cn: 孩子们整夜抱着他们的毛绒熊。

examples.en: Guests were welcomed into a plush room with leather sofas.
examples.cn: 客人们被迎进一间摆着皮沙发的豪华房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑拉什」——一把扑进长绒沙发里，「扑」的一下被柔软的毛包住，那就是 plush 的舒服；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pilus（毛发）一般认为经法语 peluche、pluche（长毛织物）进入英语 plush，核心义「长满软毛的织物」，后引申为柔软与奢华。

sensesIntro.en: Plush begins as the fabric, then its products, then the feel of softness, and finally the luxury that soft costly cloth once showed: comfort, showiness, and wealth.
sensesIntro.cn: plush 先从织物出发，再指织物制品，接着指厚软的触感，最后落到昂贵软布所象征的奢华：舒适、浮华与富有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red velvet sofa whose long pile falls in one direction under the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张深红长绒沙发，绒毛在手下顺着一个方向倒。

branches.en: The cloth itself is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 织物本身是最早的义项。

branches.en: Goods made from the cloth carry the name further.
branches.cn: 用这种布做成的物件把这个名字继续带下去。

branches.en: The soft touch is the adjective sense taken straight from the fabric.
branches.cn: 柔软触感是直接从织物取来的形容词义项。

branches.en: Comfort and wealth share the image of costly softness.
branches.cn: 舒适与富有共享「昂贵柔软」这一图像。

branches.en: Luxury becomes excess when the show of comfort goes too far.
branches.cn: 当舒适的展示过了头，奢华就变成浮华。

intro.en: Plush is a French loanword with little English suffix building beyond -y, -ness and -ly, and no obvious prefix signs.
intro.cn: plush 是法语借词，英语里除 -y、-ness、-ly 之外少有后缀构词，也没有明显的前缀成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin anchor is pilus, a hair, which lies behind French pluche and later English plush.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语锚点是 pilus（毛发），它在法语 pluche 与后来的英语 plush 背后。

items.example: Pilus is the hair image behind the fabric.
items.exampleCN: pilus 是这种织物背后的「毛发」意象。

items.example: Peluche is the older French form.
items.exampleCN: peluche 是较早的法语形式。

items.example: Pluche is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: pluche 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -y forms plushy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 plushy。

items.example: Plushy keeps the fabric quality.
items.exampleCN: plushy 保留织物的质感。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms plushness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 plushness。

items.example: Plushness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: plushness 表示这种性质。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms plushly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 plushly。

items.example: The suffix -ish can form plushish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 可以构成 plushish。

definition_zh: 变温动物；冷血动物；体温随环境变化而变化的生物
definition_en: an animal whose body temperature changes with the temperature of its surroundings rather than staying fixed
core_image: 一只蜥蜴清晨趴在石头上一动不动，靠太阳把身体慢慢晒热
scene: 沙漠的清晨，一只蜥蜴把自己摊平在晒得发烫的岩石上。Because a lizard is a poikilotherm, it must bask on warm rocks to raise its body heat each morning.
sceneCN: 这里 poikilotherm 是「变温动物」（第 1 个义项：体温随环境变化的动物）；句意：因为蜥蜴是变温动物，它每天早晨都得趴在晒热的岩石上提高体温。

pos.zh: 变温动物；体温随环境变化者

derivatives.zh: 由 poikilotherm 加 -ic 构成形容词，指「变温的」
由 poikilotherm 改尾 -y 构成，指「变温性」这一生理特性
加 -al 构成的同义形容词，指体温随环境变化的
同用希腊语 poikilo-（变化）构成，指植物含水量随环境波动的特性

senses.title: An animal whose body temperature varies
senses.definition: an animal whose internal body temperature follows the temperature of its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 身体内部温度随周围环境温度而变化的动物
senses.example: Frogs are poikilotherms and slow down in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙是变温动物，天气一冷就变得迟钝。
senses.why: Greek poikilos means varied or changing, and therme means heat, so the word literally points to heat that changes.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poikilos 意为「多变的」，therme 意为「热」，所以这个词字面上就指向「会变化的热」。

senses.title: The everyday term cold-blooded animal
senses.definition: the common name for a poikilotherm, an animal described as cold-blooded because it cannot hold a steady internal heat
senses.definitionCN: 变温动物的通俗说法，因为无法保持稳定的体内热量而被称为冷血动物
senses.example: Fish are cold-blooded, and so are all other poikilotherms.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼是冷血的，其他所有变温动物也都是。
senses.why: Popular speech took the changing body heat of these animals and called it being cold, so the technical word and the everyday phrase came to mean the same group.
senses.whyCN: 通俗说法把这些动物多变的身体热量说成「冷」，于是专业的变温一词和平常的冷血一词指同一群动物。

senses.title: A contrast with warm-blooded animals
senses.titleCN: 与恒温动物相对的一类
senses.definition: a term used to contrast these animals with endotherms, which keep a nearly constant body temperature using their own heat production
senses.definitionCN: 用于与恒温动物（靠自身产热保持几乎恒定体温的动物）相对照的术语
senses.example: Unlike a mouse, a poikilotherm cannot hold a steady internal temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 与老鼠不同，变温动物无法保持稳定的内部温度。
senses.why: The word was created as a technical label for one side of a pair, so saying poikilotherm is also saying what it is not.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是为成对概念中一边而造的技术标签，所以说「变温动物」时也在说它不是什么。

senses.title: An animal that changes temperature on purpose
senses.titleCN: 行为性调温的变温动物
senses.definition: an animal that raises or lowers its own temperature by behaviour such as basking or seeking shade, even though its basic body heat follows the environment
senses.definitionCN: 靠晒太阳或寻找阴凉等行为来升高或降低温度的动物，尽管其基础体温仍随环境变化
senses.example: A desert lizard is a poikilotherm that basks to warm itself.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠蜥蜴是一种通过晒太阳来取暖的变温动物。
senses.why: Careful study showed that changing temperature does not mean being helpless, so the technical word grew to describe deliberate behavioural warming.
senses.whyCN: 细致观察表明「体温会变」不等于「束手无策」，于是这个词又扩展出「主动通过行为调温」的意思。

senses.title: Loosely, a sluggish or adaptable creature
senses.titleCN: 广义解读：迟缓或能适应环境的生物
senses.definition: in loose or unscientific use, any creature described as sluggish in the cold or able to adapt to a wide range of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在宽松或不严谨的用法中，泛指遇冷变得迟缓、或能适应广泛条件的生物
senses.example: In old articles, any slow fish was loosely called a poikilotherm.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧文献里，任何慢吞吞的鱼都被轻率地称为变温动物。
senses.why: The picture of an animal that nearly stops when it is cold encouraged a loose wider use, which careful writers now avoid.
senses.whyCN: 「一冷就几乎停摆」的画面促使了这个宽泛的引申，现在的严谨写作者会避免这样用。

intro.en: Poikilotherm is a modern scientific compound built from two Greek words: poikilos, varied or changing, and thermē, heat.
intro.cn: poikilotherm 是现代科学复合词，由两个希腊词拼成：poikilos（多变的）与 thermē（热）。

items.en: Poikilos means varied, many-coloured or changing, and thermē means heat or warmth.
items.cn: 希腊语 poikilos 意为多样的、杂色的、变化的，thermē 意为热、温暖。

items.en: Scientists formed poikilotherm from the Greek pieces to label animals whose body heat follows the surroundings.
items.cn: 十九世纪科学家用这些希腊成分造出 poikilotherm，用来标记体温随环境变化的动物。

items.en: The word was taken into English technical writing, often paired with endotherm, an animal that heats itself.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语科学写作，常与 endotherm（靠自身产热的动物）对举使用。

items.en: The adjective poikilothermic and the noun poikilothermy spread in biology textbooks and ecology.
items.cn: 形容词 poikilothermic 与名词 poikilothermy 在生物学教科书和生态学中普及开来。

items.en: The form is now mostly technical, while the everyday phrase cold-blooded animal does the popular work.
items.cn: 如今这个词形基本限于专业领域，日常表达则由 cold-blooded animal 承担。

note.en: Poikilotherm sits in a technical family with its adjectives and nouns, and near other biology words for body heat and for adaptability.
note.cn: poikilotherm 与它自己的形容词、名词组成技术词族，并与表示体温、适应性的其他生物学词相邻。

entries.definition: having a body temperature that changes with the environment
entries.definitionCN: 体温随环境变化的

entries.definition: the condition of having a variable body temperature
entries.definitionCN: 变温性；体温可变的状态

entries.definition: an abnormally shaped blood cell, using the same changing piece
entries.definitionCN: 形状异常的细胞，使用同一个「多变」的希腊语成分

entries.definition: an animal that relies mainly on outside heat rather than its own
entries.definitionCN: 主要依靠外部热源而非自身产热的动物

entries.definition: an animal that generates its own heat and keeps a steady temperature
entries.definitionCN: 自身产热并保持稳定体温的动物

entries.definition: an animal that passes winter in a deep resting state
entries.definitionCN: 以冬眠状态度过冬天的动物

normalIntro.en: Poikilotherm is a Greek-built word: poikilo- says changing and -therm says heat, so the meaning is heat that changes.
normalIntro.cn: poikilotherm 是希腊语拼成的词：poikilo- 表示「变化」，-therm 表示「热」，合起来就是「会变化的热」。

normal.en: The stem poikilo- appears in poikilothermy and poikilocyte, always carrying the idea of varied forms.
normal.cn: 词干 poikilo- 出现在 poikilothermy 与 poikilocyte 中，始终带有「形态多变」的意思。

normal.en: The same -therm appears in thermometer, thermal and thermos.
normal.cn: 同一个 -therm 也出现在 thermometer、thermal 与 thermos 里。

normal.en: Poikilothermic is the adjective and poikilothermy is the quality, like hypothermic and hypothermia.
normal.cn: poikilothermic 是形容词，poikilothermy 表示这种性质，类比 hypothermic 与 hypothermia。

normal.en: The opposite word endotherm uses endo-, meaning inside, so its heat is made on the inside.
normal.cn: 反义词 endotherm 使用 endo-（内部），说明它的热是在身体内部产生的。

normal.en: Ectotherm and poikilotherm are close, but ectotherm stresses where the heat comes from.
normal.cn: ectotherm 与 poikilotherm 很近，但 ectotherm 强调的是热从哪里来。

abstract.en: Picture a lizard on a warm stone, its body heat rising as long as the sun stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜥蜴趴在温热的石头上，只要太阳还在，它的体温就一直在升。

abstract.en: Think of a thermometer lying in a garden and simply following the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计放在花园里，自己并不发热，只是跟着天气读数。

abstract.en: See a frog go stiff and slow as winter comes, because its heat has gone down.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天来临，青蛙因身上热量降下去而变得僵硬迟缓。

examples.en: A poikilotherm depends on its surroundings for body heat.
examples.cn: 变温动物的体温依赖周围环境。

examples.en: Most reptiles are poikilotherms, which is why they seek sunny spots.
examples.cn: 大多数爬行动物是变温动物，所以才寻找向阳的地方。

examples.en: The paper compares a poikilotherm with a small endotherm.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把一个变温动物和一种小型恒温动物作比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼其一了瑟母」——别跟这个谐音较真，只要记住「泡基楼＋热的」，泡在暖阳里才热，离开就凉，正是变温之道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 poikilos（多变的、杂色的）+ thermē（热）→ 新拉丁学术词 poikilotherm，核心义「体温随环境变化的一类动物」。

sensesIntro.en: Poikilotherm begins as the technical name for an animal with changing body heat, then meets the everyday cold-blooded label, then sits as the opposite of endotherm, then covers behavioural warming, and finally a loose wider use.
sensesIntro.cn: poikilotherm 先是「体温会变的动物」这一技术名称，再与通俗的冷血说法合流，成为恒温动物的对照项，随后扩展出「行为性调温」，最后有一个宽泛的引申用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lizard lying flat on a sun-warmed stone to raise its body heat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蜥蜴平趴在晒热的石头上提高体温。

branches.en: The scientific core is an animal with variable heat.
branches.cn: 科学核心义是「体温可变的动物」。

branches.en: The popular cold-blooded label names the same group.
branches.cn: 通俗的冷血说法指的也是同一群动物。

branches.en: The term lives as the partner of endotherm in careful contrast.
branches.cn: 这个词作为恒温动物的对照项而存在。

branches.en: Behavioural warming refines the plain idea of variable heat.
branches.cn: 行为性调温细化了对「体温可变」的朴素理解。

branches.en: The cold, slow picture of these animals feeds the loose everyday use.
branches.cn: 这些动物遇冷变慢的画面催生了宽松的日常用法。

intro.en: Poikilotherm is a Greek compound: poikilo- means varied or changing, -therm means heat, and -ic, -my and -al build its adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: poikilotherm 是希腊语复合词：poikilo- 表示多变，-therm 表示热，再由 -ic、-my、-al 构成它的形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek, not Latin, but Latin scientific writing fixed its shape, using Greek roots in a Latin spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语而非拉丁语，但拉丁语的学术写作固定了它的形态，用拉丁拼写书写希腊词根。

items.example: The Greek prefix poikilo- carries the idea of variety.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语前缀 poikilo- 表达多样的意思。

items.example: Poikilos is the source of the prefix.
items.exampleCN: poikilos 是这个词缀的来源。

items.example: The root -therm appears in thermometer and thermal.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -therm 出现在 thermometer 与 thermal 中。

items.example: Thermē is the Greek noun for heat.
items.exampleCN: thermē 是希腊语的「热」。

items.example: Poikilotherm joins the two Greek pieces.
items.exampleCN: poikilotherm 把两个希腊成分合在一起。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms poikilothermic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 poikilothermic。

items.example: Poikilothermic describes the condition.
items.exampleCN: poikilothermic 描述这种状态。

items.example: The suffix -my forms poikilothermy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -my 构成 poikilothermy。

items.meaning: the quality of variable body heat
items.example: Poikilothermy names the quality.
items.exampleCN: poikilothermy 表示这种性质。

items.example: The prefix ecto- forms ectotherm for contrast.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ecto- 构成对照用的 ectotherm。

definition_zh: 镇定自若；沉着的举止；平衡；使悬置
definition_en: calm dignity and control in the way one behaves; also balance, and to hold something suspended
core_image: 一杆天平两端砝码刚好相当，横梁停在正中，微微不动
scene: 记者的话筒挤到面前，她仍站得笔直，声音平稳。Even with microphones pushed into her face, she answered every question with remarkable poise.
sceneCN: 这里 poise 是「镇定自若」（第 1 个义项：在压力下举止沉稳）；句意：即使话筒都挤到面前，她仍以非凡的镇定回答每个问题。

collocations.zh: 失去镇定（本意：失去一个人的镇定）
把笔悬在纸上（准备落笔）

derivatives.zh: 由 poise 加 -ed 构成，义为「从容的；作好准备的」
由 poise 加 -ing 构成，义为「悬置；保持平衡」，较为少用
poise 加否定前缀 un-，义为「不拘谨的；不镇定的」，较少使用

senses.title: Calm dignity under pressure
senses.definition: a calm and confident manner, especially when others are watching or the situation is tense
senses.definitionCN: 在他人注视或局势紧张时表现出的沉着自信的举止
senses.example: She answered the hostile questions with poise.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉着地回应了那些充满敌意的问题。
senses.why: The old verb meant to weigh or balance, so a poised person is one whose inner scales have settled.
senses.whyCN: 古动词义为「称量、使平衡」，所以镇定的人就是内心天平已停稳的人。

senses.title: Graceful way of holding oneself
senses.definition: a graceful, self-assured way of standing, moving, or carrying oneself
senses.definitionCN: 站立、行走或身体姿态上的优雅自信
senses.example: The dancer moved across the stage with natural poise.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者以自然的仪态穿过舞台。
senses.why: If the body is balanced, the way it stands and moves becomes visibly graceful.
senses.whyCN: 身体一旦处于平衡，站立和移动的姿态就会显得优雅。

senses.title: Physical balance
senses.definition: the state of being balanced or held steady, especially in the body or a structure
senses.definitionCN: 身体或结构处于平衡、稳定的状态
senses.example: He kept his poise on the narrow ledge.
senses.exampleCN: 他在狭窄的岩檐上保持住了平衡。
senses.why: The Latin verb pensare means to weigh, and a balanced body is literally weighed evenly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 pensare 意为「称量」，平衡的身体字面上就是两端等重。

senses.title: To hold something suspended
senses.definition: to hold something in a fixed position, often just above or in front of something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某物固定在某一位置，常指悬在某物上方或前方
senses.example: She poised the pen above the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把笔悬在纸页上方。
senses.why: A held object sits at the balance point, neither falling nor moving, which turns the noun image back into a verb.
senses.whyCN: 悬停的物体正处于平衡点，既不下落也不移动，名词意象于是又变回动词。

senses.title: Balanced readiness
senses.definition: the condition of being balanced and ready to act at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 处于平衡状态、随时可以行动的情形
senses.example: The team is poised to win the final.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍已蓄势待发，准备赢下决赛。
senses.why: Something perfectly balanced can move in any direction at once, so poise came to mean poised for action.
senses.whyCN: 完全平衡之物可以立刻向任何方向移动，所以 poise 也引申为「蓄势待发」。

senses.title: Composure in speech and bearing
senses.definition: a composed and dignified manner of speaking and behaving in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公众场合谈话与举止的从容庄重
senses.example: Her poise on stage impressed the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上的沉稳给全场观众留下深刻印象。
senses.why: Once the balance sense is felt in the body, it also describes the steady way a person speaks and carries themselves.
senses.whyCN: 平衡义一旦落实到身体上，也能形容一个人说话和举止的稳健。

intro.en: Poise comes from Old French pois or poise, meaning weight, from Latin pensum, something weighed, from pendere, to hang or weigh.
intro.cn: poise 来自古法语 pois（重量）或 poise，源头是拉丁语 pensum（称过的东西），出自 pendere（悬挂、称量）。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or to weigh, and pensum is something weighed out.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂或称量，pensum 指称量出的一份。

items.en: Pois and poise mean weight or a weight used for balancing.
items.cn: pois 与 poise 指重量或用于平衡的砝码。

items.en: Poise first names a weight on scales and also a balance or equipoise.
items.cn: 中古英语早期，poise 指天平上的砝码，也指平衡状态。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense to balance or hold something steady.
items.cn: 动词义在十六世纪出现，义为「使平衡、稳稳持住」。

items.en: The figurative sense of calm self-control becomes the most common use.
items.cn: 现代英语中，「冷静自持」的比喻义成为最常用的义项。

note.en: Poise is the noun of balance, close to poised, composure, and to calm words such as assurance and equanimity.
note.cn: poise 是表示「平衡」的名词，与 poised、composure 以及 assurance、equanimity 等「沉着」类词相邻。

entries.definition: calm and confident, or ready to act
entries.definitionCN: 沉着的；蓄势待发的

entries.definition: a state of even balance
entries.definitionCN: 平衡；均势

entries.definition: a position held for a picture, or an act of pretending
entries.definitionCN: 姿势；装样子（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 ponere，意为放置）

entries.definition: the state of being calm and in control of oneself
entries.definitionCN: 镇静；沉着

entries.definition: confident belief in ones own ability
entries.definitionCN: 自信；把握

entries.definition: calm temper under strain
entries.definitionCN: （压力下的）平静；沉着

normalIntro.en: Poise is a balance of body and mind: the old word for a weight on a scale later came to mean a steady person.
normalIntro.cn: poise 是身与心的平衡：这个原本指「秤上砝码」的旧词，后来用来形容沉稳的人。

normal.en: With poise means calmly and confidently.
normal.cn: with poise 表示沉着自信地。

normal.en: To lose ones poise is to become flustered.
normal.cn: 失去镇定，就是变得慌乱。

normal.en: A speaker with remarkable poise does not rush words.
normal.cn: 极具镇定的演讲者不会抢话。

normal.en: Compare balanced: balanced is the plain word, poise is its polished, formal cousin.
normal.cn: 对比 balanced：balanced 是普通说法，poise 是其更精致、更正式的对应词。

normal.en: The adjective poised is far more common than the noun in everyday speech.
normal.cn: 口语中形容词 poised 比名词 poise 常见得多。

abstract.en: Picture a tightrope walker frozen for a second, perfectly level.
abstract.cn: 想象走钢丝的人在半空停住一秒，身体完全水平。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass of water carried so steadily that the surface does not tremble.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水被端得极稳，水面一点不晃。

abstract.en: Think of a scale beam resting exactly in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象天平横梁恰好停在正中央。

examples.en: The young athlete showed great poise after the defeat.
examples.cn: 这位年轻运动员失利后表现得十分镇定。

examples.en: She never lost her poise during the long meeting.
examples.cn: 在漫长的会议中，她始终没有失去镇定。

examples.en: He poised the camera on the rail and waited.
examples.cn: 他把相机稳稳架在栏杆上，等待时机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破椅子」——椅子破了还坐得稳稳当当，就是 poise 的那份镇定；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称量）→ pensum（称出的一份）→ 古法语 pois、poise（重量；砝码）→ 英语 poise，核心义「天平两端相称」。

sensesIntro.en: Poise starts from weighing: a weight on a scale becomes balance, then a steady body, and finally a calm mind.
sensesIntro.cn: poise 从称量出发：秤上的砝码先变成平衡，再变成稳健的身体，最后落到沉着的内心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale beam resting perfectly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平横梁恰好停在水平位置。

branches.en: A mind whose scales are level shows calm dignity.
branches.cn: 内心的天平不偏不倚，就表现为镇定自若。

branches.en: A balanced body moves gracefully.
branches.cn: 平衡的身体移动起来优雅。

branches.en: The literal sense is simply balance.
branches.cn: 字面义就是平衡本身。

branches.en: Something held at the balance point hangs suspended.
branches.cn: 放在平衡点上的东西就是悬置的。

branches.en: Balanced and ready means poised, and poise shows in speech and bearing.
branches.cn: 平衡且随时可动就是蓄势待发，而沉着也体现在谈吐与举止中。

intro.en: Poise comes through French from the Latin weighing root pensum and pendere, which also gives pendant, pension, and pendulum.
intro.cn: poise 经法语来自拉丁语中表示「称量」的 pensum 与 pendere，同一词根还派生出 pendant、pension 与 pendulum。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere means to hang or weigh, and pensum is what has been weighed out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂或称量，pensum 指称量好的一份。

items.example: Pendere gives the hanging and weighing sense.
items.exampleCN: pendere 提供「悬挂与称量」的含义。

items.example: Pensum links the word to weight.
items.exampleCN: pensum 把词与重量联系起来。

items.example: Pois carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: pois 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms poised.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 poised。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unpoised.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unpoised。

items.example: Pendant keeps the hanging sense.
items.exampleCN: pendant 保留了「悬挂」义。

items.example: Pendulum balances while hanging.
items.exampleCN: pendulum 悬挂中保持平衡。

items.example: Equipoise adds the idea of equality.
items.exampleCN: equipoise 加上「相等」的意思。

items.meaning: a regular payment, originally a weighed payment
items.meaningCN: 养老金（原意为按份称出的供给）
items.example: Pension goes back to the same weighing root.
items.exampleCN: pension 也追溯到同一「称量」词根。

definition_zh: 北极星；指路明灯；为人追随的核心
definition_en: the North Star, used to find the north; also a guide or principle that people follow
core_image: 夜空中央一颗不动的星，四周群星缓缓环绕它旋转
scene: 夜里迷路的人抬头找到那颗不动的小星，便认出了北方。Sailors lost in the dark looked up and found their way by the polestar.
sceneCN: 这里 polestar 是「北极星」（第 1 个义项：用以指示正北方向的恒星）；句意：黑暗中迷路的水手抬头，靠北极星找到方向。

pos.zh: 北极星；指路明灯；追随的核心

collocations.zh: 跟随北极星；以之为指引

derivatives.zh: 同源基础词，义为「地轴的一端；极点」，polestar 围绕它构成
pole 的复数，义为「两极」，与 polestar 共享词根
由词素 star 加 -y 构成，义为「布满星星的」，与 polestar 同词族
star 加后缀 -less 构成，义为「没有星星的」，可作对照记忆

senses.title: The North Star
senses.definition: the bright star near the north celestial pole that appears to stay almost still and shows the direction of north
senses.definitionCN: 位于北天极附近的亮星，看上去几乎不动，用来指示正北方向
senses.example: Ancient sailors steered by the polestar.
senses.exampleCN: 古代水手靠北极星辨别航向。
senses.why: Pole names the point the earth turns around, and a star is a fixed light, so the compound means the star marking the pole.
senses.whyCN: pole 指地球自转所绕的那一点，star 是固定的光点，合成词就指「标志天极的那颗星」。

senses.title: A guiding principle
senses.definition: a principle, belief, or aim that guides a person or group like a fixed star
senses.definitionCN: 像不动的星辰一样指引个人或群体的原则、信念或目标
senses.example: Honesty was the polestar of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 诚信是她事业上的指路明灯。
senses.why: A star that never moves gives direction to travellers, so any fixed rule that guides conduct takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 永不移动的星辰为旅人指引方向，所以任何指导行为的固定准则都借用了这个名字。

senses.title: The fixed centre of attention
senses.definition: the person, idea, or thing that everything else is organized around or turns to for direction
senses.definitionCN: 其他事物围绕其组织、向其寻求方向的人、观念或事物
senses.example: The small library became the polestar of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小图书馆成了全村人追随的核心。
senses.why: Other stars seem to circle the polestar, so the word extends to whatever others revolve around.
senses.whyCN: 群星仿佛绕着北极星转，于是这个词也扩展到其他事物所环绕的中心。

senses.title: The star that itself keeps its pole
senses.definition: the star that lies closest to one of the celestial poles at a given period, which changes slowly over centuries
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时期最靠近天极的恒星，这一身份会随世纪缓慢更替
senses.example: Polaris is not the polestar forever.
senses.exampleCN: 北极星并非永远是那颗极点星。
senses.why: Earth tilts slowly, so the point the sky turns about drifts, and other stars take the role in turn.
senses.whyCN: 地轴缓慢摆动，天空旋转的中心随之漂移，别的恒星会轮流担任这一角色。

senses.title: A beacon of hope
senses.definition: something that gives steady hope or encouragement to people in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 在困境中给人稳定希望或鼓励的事物
senses.example: For the refugees, news reports were a polestar of hope.
senses.exampleCN: 对流亡者来说，新闻报道是希望的灯塔。
senses.why: The star is brightest in the dark, so the image naturally shifts from direction to hope in hard times.
senses.whyCN: 星辰在黑暗中最为明亮，意象于是从「方向」自然过渡到「困境中的希望」。

intro.en: Polestar is an English compound of pole, from Greek polos, a pivot or axis, and star, from Old English steorra, and has named the guiding northern star since the late Middle Ages.
intro.cn: polestar 是英语合成词，由 pole（源自希腊语 polos，意为枢轴）与 star（源自中古英语 steorra）组成，自中古后期起用来指指引方向的北方星。

items.en: Polos means a pivot or axis, the point around which something turns.
items.cn: polos 意为枢轴，即某物绕之旋转的点。

items.en: Polus carries the axis sense and develops the astronomical meaning.
items.cn: polus 继承「轴」义，并发展出天文学上的含义。

items.en: Pole is used for the end of the earth axis and for the pole of the heavens.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，pole 既指地轴的一端，也指天球的极点。

items.en: The two nouns are joined in writing as pole star for the guiding northern star.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，二者连写为 pole star，专门指起导航作用的北方星。

items.en: The compound is spelled polestar and takes the figurative sense of a guiding principle.
items.cn: 现代英语写成 polestar，并获得「指导原则」的比喻义。

note.en: Polestar names the star used as a fixed guide; it neighbours pole, star words, and the whole family of guide and beacon terms.
note.cn: polestar 指用作固定指引的星辰，与 pole、各类 star 词以及整套「指引、灯塔」类词相邻。

entries.definition: either end of the earth axis, or a long thin stick
entries.definitionCN: 地轴的一端，或细长的木杆

entries.definition: relating to the poles or to the North or South Pole
entries.definitionCN: 极地的；两极的

entries.definition: the two poles of the earth or of a magnet
entries.definitionCN: （地球或磁体的）两极（与 polestar 同源词，复数形式）

entries.definition: a star used as a guide, or a guiding principle
entries.definitionCN: 指路星；指导原则

entries.definition: a light or signal that guides or warns
entries.definitionCN: 灯塔；信标

entries.definition: the direction the polestar shows
entries.definitionCN: 北方（polestar 所指示的方向）

normalIntro.en: Polestar joins the pole of the sky to the star that sits there, so the word itself pictures a fixed point of light.
normalIntro.cn: polestar 把「天空的极点」与「坐在那里的星」合成一词，词形本身就是一幅「固定光点」的画。

normal.en: The polestar shows the way north.
normal.cn: polestar 指示向北的路。

normal.en: A polestar of study means an ideal that guides learning.
normal.cn: a polestar of study 指引领学习的目标。

normal.en: Polaris is the usual English name for the polestar today.
normal.cn: 今天英语里通常把北极星称作物名 Polaris。

normal.en: Compare lodestar: lodestar is the older sea word for the same guiding star.
normal.cn: 对比 lodestar：lodestar 是航海时代对同一指路星的旧称。

normal.en: The polestar is a compound of pole and star, so both halves carry meaning.
normal.cn: polestar 由 pole 与 star 合成，两半各自表义。

abstract.en: Picture a still point in a sky that spins around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片旋转的夜空中央有个静止的光点。

abstract.en: Imagine a traveller in a dark plain, eyes fixed on one star.
abstract.cn: 想象黑夜里旅人站在旷野，目光锁定一颗星。

abstract.en: Think of an old compass whose needle always points to the same spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚旧罗盘，指针永远指向同一处。

examples.en: The polestar was a navigators best friend on a clear night.
examples.cn: 在晴朗的夜里，北极星是航海者最好的伙伴。

examples.en: Care for the poor was the polestar of his long career.
examples.cn: 关心穷人是漫长事业中的指路明灯。

examples.en: Children looked up to find the polestar above the hills.
examples.cn: 孩子们抬头找山峦上方的北极星。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡上star」——山坡上挂着的一颗星，为走夜路的人指北；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 polos（枢轴、天极）→ 拉丁语 polus（极）→ 英语 pole（极点）+ 中古英语 steorra（星）→ pole star → polestar，核心义「天极上不动的星」。

sensesIntro.en: Polestar begins with a real star at the top of the sky and then borrows its fixity for rules, centres of attention, and hope.
sensesIntro.cn: polestar 先指天顶上一颗真实的星，再把它的「不动」借给准则、核心与希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one star that never moves while the sky turns around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜空中一颗不动的星，群星绕其旋转。

branches.en: The literal sense is the star near the north pole of the sky.
branches.cn: 字面义就是靠近北天极的那颗星。

branches.en: A principle that does not shift guides like that star.
branches.cn: 不变的准则像那颗星一样指引方向。

branches.en: What others revolve around becomes the centre.
branches.cn: 其他事物所环绕者便成为核心。

branches.en: The pole itself drifts, so the role passes between stars.
branches.cn: 极点本身在漂移，所以这一角色会在星辰间更替。

branches.en: A light in the dark gives direction and also hope.
branches.cn: 黑暗中的光既给方向也给希望。

intro.en: Polestar is a two-part compound: the Greek-derived pole of axis and poles, and the Germanic star shared with starry and starlight.
intro.cn: polestar 是双词素合成词：一半是源自希腊语、表示「轴与极点」的 pole，另一半是日耳曼语的 star，与 starry、starlight 同族。

latinIntro.en: Greek polos, a pivot, becomes Latin polus, the pole of the heavens, and then English pole.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 polos（枢轴）变成拉丁语 polus（天极），再进入英语成为 pole。

items.example: Polos gives the turning point image.
items.exampleCN: polos 提供「转轴」的意象。

items.meaning: the end of an axis, the pole of the heavens
items.example: Polus moves the sense to the sky.
items.exampleCN: polus 把词义移向天空。

items.meaning: either end of the earth axis
items.example: Pole is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: pole 是合成词的前半。

items.example: Steorra is the ancestor of star.
items.exampleCN: steorra 是 star 的前身。

items.meaning: a fixed point of light in the night sky
items.example: Star is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: star 是合成词的后半。

items.example: The suffix -y forms starry.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 starry。

items.example: The suffix -less forms starless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 starless。

items.example: The suffix -ar forms polar.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ar 构成 polar。

items.example: Lodestar is a near cousin of polestar.
items.exampleCN: lodestar 是 polestar 的近亲词。

latinEntries.meaning: the pole of the heavens, the end of an axis

definition_zh: 花粉；授粉用的细粉
definition_en: the fine powder produced by flowers that carries male cells and fertilizes seeds
core_image: 蜜蜂后腿上黏着一团黄澄澄的细粉，从一朵花飞向另一朵花
scene: 春天风一吹，空气里飘着细细的黄粉，过敏的人不停打喷嚏。In spring the wind lifts fine yellow pollen and everyone with an allergy starts sneezing.
sceneCN: 这里 pollen 是「花粉」（第 1 个义项：花朵产生的细粉）；句意：春天风把黄色的细花粉扬起，有过敏的人不停打喷嚏。

collocations.zh: 空气中花粉数（花粉指数）

derivatives.zh: 由 pollen 加 -ate 构成，义为「给……授粉」
pollinate 加 -ion 构成，义为「传粉；授粉」
pollinate 加 -or 构成，义为「传粉者；传粉昆虫」
医学用语，由 pollin- 加 -osis 构成，义为「花粉症」

senses.title: The fine powder of flowers
senses.definition: the fine powdery grains produced in the male parts of flowers, which carry the male cells
senses.definitionCN: 花的雄性部分产生的细粉状颗粒，携带雄性细胞
senses.example: Bees collect pollen and use it as food.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂采集花粉并把它当作食物。
senses.why: Latin pollen meant fine meal or dust, and the yellowish flower dust looked just like what a mill sifts out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pollen 意为细面粉或尘土，而黄色的花尘正像磨坊筛出的细粉。

senses.title: The carrier of plant reproduction
senses.definition: the material that moves male cells from one flower to another so that seeds can form
senses.definitionCN: 把雄性细胞从一朵花送到另一朵花，使种子得以形成的物质
senses.example: Wind blows pollen from one field to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 风把花粉从一块田地吹到另一块。
senses.why: Because the powder carries cells, the word also names the whole transport of plant reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 因为这粉末携带细胞，这个词也指植物繁殖的整个运输过程。

senses.title: A cause of seasonal allergy
senses.definition: the grains from trees, grasses, and weeds that trigger sneezing and watery eyes in sensitive people
senses.definitionCN: 树木、草类和杂草的花粉，在敏感人群中引发打喷嚏和流泪
senses.example: Her eyes water whenever high pollen levels are reported.
senses.exampleCN: 只要预报花粉浓度高，她的眼睛就流泪。
senses.why: Fine dust is easy to inhale, so the same powder that fertilizes flowers also irritates noses.
senses.whyCN: 细粉容易被吸入，因此给花授粉的粉末同样会刺激鼻子。

senses.title: Any fine powdery mass
senses.definition: a very fine powder, in old or poetic use
senses.definitionCN: 极细的粉末，多用于旧式或诗歌语境
senses.example: A pale pollen of dust lay on the old books.
senses.exampleCN: 旧书上一层灰白的尘粉。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense, a fine meal, kept alive in literary English.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义「细面」，在文学英语中一直被保留着。

senses.title: The dust that marks pollen season
senses.definition: the pollen visible in the air and on surfaces during the flowering season
senses.definitionCN: 开花季节飘在空气中、落在物体表面上的花粉
senses.example: A fine yellow pollen covered every car in the street.
senses.exampleCN: 街上每辆汽车都覆着一层黄色的细花粉。
senses.why: The dust sense of the word makes it easy to describe pollen as something that visibly settles on the world.
senses.whyCN: 「灰尘」这一层词义使 pollen 常被写成落满世界的东西。

intro.en: Pollen is Latin for fine flour or dust, from the verb pollere, to be strong or fine, and it entered English botany as the name of the flower dust.
intro.cn: pollen 是拉丁语「细面粉、尘土」之意，出自动词 pollere（强健、精细），进入英语植物学后专指花中的细粉。

items.en: Pollen means fine flour or dust, and pollere means to be strong or powerful.
items.cn: pollen 意为细面粉或尘土，pollere 意为强健有力。

items.en: Botanists use pollen for the fertilizing dust of flowers, a revival of the old dust sense.
items.cn: 植物学家用 pollen 指花朵的受精细粉，是旧「尘粉」义的复活。

items.en: The word enters English scientific writing in the shape pollen.
items.cn: 十七世纪该词以 pollen 的形式进入英语科学文献。

items.en: Linnaeus and later writers fix pollen as the standard botanical term.
items.cn: 林奈及后来作者把 pollen 固定为标准植物学术语。

items.en: The verb pollinate and the noun pollination grow from it, and allergy writing spreads the word to medicine.
items.cn: 动词 pollinate 与名词 pollination 由此派生，医学中的过敏文献又把它带入日常。

note.en: Pollen is the fine dust of flowers; it is linked by form and root to pollinate and pollution words, and by meaning to seed and nectar terms.
note.cn: pollen 指花中的细粉，在形与根上与 pollinate、pollution 类词相近，在义上与 seed、nectar 等词同场。

entries.definition: to put pollen onto a flower so that it can form seeds
entries.definitionCN: 给花授粉，使其能结出种子

entries.definition: the process of moving pollen between flowers
entries.definitionCN: 花之间传递花粉的过程

entries.definition: harmful waste in the air, water, or soil
entries.definitionCN: 污染（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 polluere，意为弄脏）

entries.definition: the sweet liquid in flowers that draws insects
entries.definitionCN: 花中吸引昆虫的甜液

entries.definition: the small part of a plant from which a new plant grows
entries.definitionCN: 能长出新植物的种子

entries.definition: the part of a flower that makes pollen
entries.definitionCN: 花中产生花粉的花药

normalIntro.en: Pollen was Latin dust, so the flower powder is simply fine dust with a job to do.
normalIntro.cn: pollen 在拉丁语里就是「细面、尘土」，所以花粉不过是带着任务的细粉。

normal.en: Each pollen grain is far too small to see clearly.
normal.cn: 每粒花粉都小得看不清。

normal.en: Bees transfer pollen from flower to flower.
normal.cn: 蜜蜂在花与花之间传递花粉。

normal.en: A pollen allergy is often called hay fever.
normal.cn: 花粉过敏常被称作枯草热。

normal.en: Compare pollen and pollination: pollen is the dust, pollination is the act of moving it.
normal.cn: 对比 pollen 与 pollination：前者是粉，后者是传粉这一动作。

normal.en: Pollen has no common verb of its own, so pollinate does the work.
normal.cn: pollen 本身没有常用动词形式，传粉的动作由 pollinate 承担。

abstract.en: Picture a bee landing with yellow dust stuck to its legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜜蜂落下，腿上沾满黄色的粉。

abstract.en: Imagine a fine golden cloud drifting from a meadow.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上飘起一层金色的细雾。

abstract.en: Think of a flour mill, because the word once meant fine flour.
abstract.cn: 想象一座磨坊，因为这个词本义是细面粉。

examples.en: Birds and insects carry pollen between flowers.
examples.cn: 鸟类和昆虫在花之间传播花粉。

examples.en: The pollen count is high today, so stay indoors if you can.
examples.cn: 今天花粉指数很高，如果可以就待在室内。

examples.en: Wind-blown pollen can travel for hundreds of kilometres.
examples.cn: 随风传播的花粉可以飘行数百公里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼冷」——风一吹，花粉像被泼开的冷水雾一样弥漫，让人打喷嚏；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pollere（强健、精细）→ pollen（细面粉；尘土）→ 植物学借用于「花中细粉」→ 英语 pollen，核心义「极细的粉末」。

sensesIntro.en: Pollen goes from Latin flour dust to flower dust, then to the carrier of reproduction, a cause of allergy, and any fine powder.
sensesIntro.cn: pollen 从拉丁语「细面粉」到「花中细粉」，再到繁殖媒介、过敏元凶与泛指细粉末。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: yellow flower dust stuck to a bee leg.
core.cn: 核心意象：蜜蜂腿上沾着的黄色花粉。

branches.en: The concrete sense is the powder made by flowers.
branches.cn: 具体义就是花产生的粉末。

branches.en: Carrying cells makes the powder a medium of reproduction.
branches.cn: 承载细胞使这粉末成为繁殖媒介。

branches.en: Fine dust in the air irritates sensitive noses.
branches.cn: 空气中的细粉会刺激敏感的鼻子。

branches.en: The old Latin sense survives as any fine powder.
branches.cn: 古老的拉丁语义作为「泛指细粉」保留下来。

branches.en: Pollen is both the powder on the bee and the dust in the season air.
branches.cn: pollen 既是蜂腿上的粉，也是季节空气中的尘。

intro.en: Pollen is a Latin borrowing with no native English prefix; its family grows through -ate, -ion, -or, and the medical -osis.
intro.cn: pollen 是拉丁语借词，没有英语本土前缀；它的词族靠 -ate、-ion、-or 与医学词尾 -osis 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin pollen means fine flour or dust, and the verb pollere means to be strong or effective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pollen 意为细面粉或尘土，动词 pollere 意为强健、有效。

items.example: Pollen is taken directly from Latin.
items.exampleCN: pollen 直接借自拉丁语。

items.example: Pollere is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: pollere 是名词背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms pollinate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 pollinate。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms pollination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 pollination。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -or forms pollinator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 pollinator。

items.example: The suffix -osis forms pollinosis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -osis 构成 pollinosis。

items.example: Pollin- appears in polliniferous.
items.exampleCN: pollin- 出现在 polliniferous 中。

items.example: The suffix -ferous forms polliniferous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ferous 构成 polliniferous。

items.example: The suffix -ation also forms pollination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 同样构成 pollination。

definition_zh: 污染者；造成污染的人、企业或国家；（生态学）污染物释放源
definition_en: a person, company, or country that makes air, water, or land dirty and unsafe
core_image: 一个人往清澈的河水里倒下一桶脏东西，水面立刻变得浑浊
scene: 河岸边堆着工厂排出的废渣，村民指着排水口，要求责任人清理干净。Villagers pointed at the drain and demanded that the polluter clean up the river.
sceneCN: 这里 polluter 是「污染者」（第 1 个义项：造成污染的人、企业或国家）；句意：村民指着排水口，要求污染者把河水清理干净。

derivatives.zh: polluter 的动词形式，去 -er，义为「污染」
由 pollute 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「污染」
由 pollute 加后缀 -ant 构成，义为「污染物」
过去分词作形容词，义为「被污染的」

senses.title: A person or organization that causes pollution
senses.definition: someone or a body that sends waste or harmful substances into air, water, or land
senses.definitionCN: 把废物或有害物质排入空气、水体或土地的人或机构
senses.example: Environmental groups blamed the factory for acting as a polluter.
senses.exampleCN: 环保组织指责这家工厂是污染者。
senses.why: Latin polluere means to soil or defile, and the -er ending names the one who does that soiling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 polluere 意为「弄脏、玷污」，-er 后缀正好称呼做这件弄脏之事的一方。

senses.title: A country or industry that emits most pollution
senses.titleCN: 排放最多污染的行业或国家
senses.definition: a country or industry that releases the largest amounts of greenhouse gases or waste
senses.definitionCN: 排放温室气体或废物最多的国家或行业
senses.example: The talks focused on the largest polluters in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈聚焦于该地区最大的排放国。
senses.why: When a whole state burns fuel for everyone, the state itself becomes the one doing the soiling.
senses.whyCN: 当一个国家替所有人烧燃料排放时，这个国家本身就成弄脏环境的一方。

senses.title: A substance or device that releases pollution
senses.titleCN: 释放污染的污染物或装置
senses.definition: a substance, machine, or leak that puts pollutants into the environment
senses.definitionCN: 向环境中释放污染物的物质、机器或泄漏点
senses.example: The old pipeline is a steady polluter of the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧管道是土壤的持续污染源。
senses.why: Once several agents carry the word, the thing that soils can also be named rather than only a person.
senses.whyCN: 既然多个词可以携带这个词，弄脏环境的那一方也可以是一件东西，而不只是一个人。

senses.title: A source of pollution in an ecosystem study
senses.titleCN: 生态系统研究中的污染源
senses.definition: the point or source from which pollution enters an ecosystem and affects plants and animals
senses.definitionCN: 污染进入生态系统并影响动植物的那个点或来源
senses.example: The river was classified as a polluter of the coastal food chain.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河被判定为沿海食物链的污染源。
senses.why: In field studies a river or a plant can be called a polluter, because the chain of harm starts there.
senses.whyCN: 在野外研究中，河流或工厂可以被称为污染源，因为受害的链条从这里开始。

senses.title: A party in a legal dispute over cleanup
senses.definition: a party involved in disputes over who must pay for the damage pollution causes
senses.definitionCN: 在污染损害由谁付费的争议中涉及的一方
senses.example: The court ruled that the chemical plant was the polluter of the aquifer.
senses.exampleCN: 法院裁定这家化工厂是地下含水层的污染者。
senses.why: In court the word names the party that must pay, so blame and legal responsibility sharpen the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上这个词指名必须付费的一方，于是责任归属让词义更锋利。

senses.title: A very dirty person or thing
senses.definition: informal: a person or creature that soils whatever it touches
senses.definitionCN: 口语：碰到什么都弄脏的人或动物
senses.example: Her puppy is a cute little polluter of every rug.
senses.exampleCN: 她的幼犬是个可爱的小捣蛋，把每块地毯都弄脏。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of defiling stays in the background, so any careless dirtying can still earn the label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「玷污」意味一直藏在背后，所以任何粗心的弄脏行为仍可能被安上这个名号。

intro.en: Polluter is a plain agent noun: the Latin verb for soiling plus the English ending -er.
intro.cn: polluter 是一个普通的施事名词：拉丁语表示「弄脏、玷污」的动词加英语后缀 -er。

items.en: The root behind Latin power is generally reconstructed as *peu- 「to clean, purify」; the deeper descent is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 power 背后的词根一般认为可重构为表示「清洁、净化」的 *peu-；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Polluere meant to soil, defile, or violate, and pulled the early sense toward the ritual idea of staining a clean thing.
items.cn: polluere 意为「弄脏、玷污、侵犯」，早期语义偏向「把干净之物玷污」的仪式性含义。

items.en: The noun pollutio covered both physical filth and religious defilement.
items.cn: 名词 pollutio 兼指身体上的污秽与宗教上的不洁。

items.en: Old French polluer brought the verb into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 polluer 于十四世纪把这个动词带入英语。

items.en: Agents formed with -er appear in the sixteenth century, and the early use often concerned tainting a good name or a record.
items.cn: 带 -er 的施事形式见于十六世纪，早期用例常指败坏名声或记录。

items.en: The environmental sense took over after the nineteenth century, and polluter now usually means a source of dirty air, water, or land.
items.cn: 十九世纪后环境义占主导，如今 polluter 通常指空气、水体或土地的污染源。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same polluere root; the near-meaning group gathers the people and things on the receiving and sending ends of pollution.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一 polluere 词根构成的形态；近义组收污染中排放与受害两端的对象。

entries.definition: the act of polluting, or the dirty state it leaves behind
entries.definitionCN: 污染的行为或造成的污染状况

entries.definition: a substance that makes air, water, or soil dirty
entries.definitionCN: 使环境变脏的物质

entries.definition: to make air, water, or land dirty and unsafe
entries.definitionCN: 污染空气、水体或土地

entries.definition: a person who votes; only the spelling is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 投票者；只是拼写接近，词源不同

entries.definition: a thing or place that sends out gases or energy
entries.definitionCN: 排放气体或能量的东西或地点

entries.definition: a substance that spoils something by mixing with it
entries.definitionCN: 混入而破坏他物的物质

entries.definition: someone or something harmed by an action; the opposite side of a polluter
entries.definitionCN: 受行为伤害的一方，与污染者相对

entries.definition: someone who breaks a rule or does wrong
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则或做错事的人

normalIntro.en: Polluter is built the ordinary way: the Latin verb for soil plus -er, so every relative in the family hides the same root.
normalIntro.cn: polluter 按最普通的方式构成：表示「弄脏」的拉丁动词加 -er，所以词族里每个成员都藏着同一个词根。

normal.en: Pollute plus -er gives the doer, polluter.
normal.cn: pollute 加 -er 就得到做这件事的一方 polluter。

normal.en: Pollution is the damage, pollutant is the substance, polluter is the one who releases it.
normal.cn: pollution 是损害，pollutant 是物质，polluter 是排放它的一方。

normal.en: The phrase the polluter pays principle names who should bear the cost.
normal.cn: the polluter pays principle 规定了该由谁承担费用。

normal.en: Latin polluere first meant to defile something sacred, a sense pollution has partly lost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 polluere 起初指玷污神圣之物，这一意味 pollution 已部分失去。

normal.en: Hold polluters accountable is the fixed phrase used in law and activism.
normal.cn: hold polluters accountable 是法律与环保活动中常用的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tipping a bucket of black oil into clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一桶黑油倒进清水。

abstract.en: Imagine a factory chimney breathing grey smoke into a clean sky.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂烟囱向洁净的天空吐着灰烟。

abstract.en: Think of a footprint left in fresh snow.
abstract.cn: 想象新雪上留下的一只脚印。

examples.en: Under the treaty, every polluter must pay for the cleanup.
examples.cn: 根据条约，每个污染者都必须为清理买单。

examples.en: The report named the ten largest industrial polluters in the country.
examples.cn: 报告列出了该国十大工业污染者。

examples.en: Coal plants are still among the biggest polluters of the air.
examples.cn: 燃煤电厂仍是最大的空气污染者之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼路特」——有人一路往路上泼脏水，把干净的路弄脏，他就是污染者；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 polluere（弄脏、玷污）→ pollutio（污秽）→ 古法语 polluer → 英语 pollute，加 -er 构成 polluter「弄脏那环境的一方」。

sensesIntro.en: Polluter starts with the person or firm that dirties the environment, widens to states and industries, then to things that leak pollution, and ends in informal use for any dirty thing.
sensesIntro.cn: polluter 先指弄脏环境的人或企业，扩大到国家与行业，再指泄漏污染的物，最后口语化地指任何脏东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pouring something filthy into clean water and the water turning cloudy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把脏东西倒进清水，水面随即变得浑浊。

branches.en: The person or firm that dirties the environment is the main sense.
branches.cn: 弄脏环境的个人或企业是主要义项。

branches.en: Whole states and industries can be polluters too.
branches.cn: 整个国家和行业也可以是污染者。

branches.en: Leaks and machines release pollution like a person.
branches.cn: 泄漏点与机器也会像人一样释放污染。

branches.en: Both name the side that sends the waste, not the side that suffers.
branches.cn: 两者都指排放废物的一方，而不是受害的一方。

branches.en: The person sense answers who must pay the bill.
branches.cn: 人的义项回答了谁该付账。

intro.en: Polluter is Latin polluere plus the English agent ending -er, and the wider family adds -tion, -ant, and -ted.
intro.cn: polluter 是拉丁语 polluere 加英语施事后缀 -er，整个词族再加 -tion、-ant、-ted。

latinIntro.en: Latin polluere and pollutio carry the defiling image from Rome into Old French and then into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 polluere 与 pollutio 把「玷污」的意象从罗马经古法语带入英语。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被弄脏的状态。

items.example: The suffix -er forms polluter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 polluter。

items.example: The verb is the base form.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是基础形式。

items.meaning: the state of being made dirty
items.example: The noun names the damage.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指损害本身。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms pollutant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 pollutant。

items.example: The adjective describes the water.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述水体。

items.example: The suffix -able is not freely used with pollute.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 一般不与 pollute 自由组合。

definition_zh: 多边形；多角形；（几何学）闭合的直线多边形
definition_en: a flat closed shape made of three or more straight sides
core_image: 一张纸上用直尺一段一段连起来的封闭折线，回到起点时围出一块地
scene: 老师在黑板上画了一个封闭的折线图，又让学生数一数它有几条边、几个角。The teacher asked the class to count the sides and corners of each polygon on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 polygon 是「多边形」（第 1 个义项：由多条直线边围成的封闭平面图形）；句意：老师让全班数一数黑板上每个多边形有几条边、几个角。

collocations.phrase: calculate the area of a polygon

derivatives.zh: 由 polygon 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「多边形的、多角形的」
常与 polygon 搭配成 regular polygon，义为「正多边形的」
与 polygon 同义的三角形系概念，义为「三角形的」
首字母大写的同形词，常见于专有名称与地图文件名

senses.title: A closed flat figure with straight sides
senses.definition: a flat shape with three or more straight sides that meet to close it completely
senses.definitionCN: 由三条或三条以上直线边首尾相接、完全闭合的平面图形
senses.example: A triangle is the polygon with the fewest sides.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形是边数最少的多边形。
senses.why: Greek poly- means many and gonia means corner, so the word literally names a many-cornered outline.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poly- 意为「多」，gonia 意为「角」，所以这个词字面就是「有很多角的轮廓」。

senses.title: A regular polygon in geometry
senses.definition: a polygon whose sides are all equal and whose angles are all equal, such as a square or a hexagon
senses.definitionCN: 各边等长、各角相等的多边形，例如正方形与正六边形
