senses.example: Each side of a regular polygon has the same length.
senses.exampleCN: 正多边形的每条边都一样长。
senses.why: Bonus geometry words attach to many-sided figures: hexagon, octagon, and equilateral all share the corner root gonia.
senses.whyCN: 多边形衍生的几何术语都长在这类多边图形上：hexagon、octagon、equilateral 共享表示「角」的 gonia 词根。

senses.title: Any many-sided outline in working jargon
senses.titleCN: 工作用语中的多边轮廓
senses.definition: a simplified, many-sided boundary of a piece of land, a plot on a map, or a zone in a computer drawing
senses.definitionCN: 地块、地图图斑或电脑绘图区域上由多段直线围成的简化边界
senses.example: The surveyor drew a polygon around the plot.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员沿着这块地画了一个多边形边界。
senses.why: Software and maps keep the literal shape but weaken the regularity: any closed straight-edged boundary gets called a polygon.
senses.whyCN: 软件与地图保留了字面形状却放宽了规则：任何由直线段围成的闭合边界都被叫作 polygon。

senses.title: A test region within a shape
senses.definition: a region enclosed by straight sides, used in tests about whether a point lies inside a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 由直线边围成的一块区域，用于判断某点是否落在边界之内
senses.example: The program checks whether the point lies inside the polygon.
senses.exampleCN: 程序检查这个点是否落在多边形内部。
senses.why: The cornered outline becomes a container: everything inside the straight lines counts as enclosed.
senses.whyCN: 有棱有角的轮廓变成了一个容器：直线围住的一切都算作「在里头」。

intro.en: Polygon is a learned Greek compound that English borrowed whole through Latin, without changing its parts: many plus corner.
intro.cn: polygon 是直接从拉丁语借入的希腊语复合词，两部分「多」与「角」都没有改变。

items.en: Greek polus meant 「much, many」 and polus-shaped forms gave English poly-, as in polyglot and polygamy.
items.cn: 希腊语 polus 意为「多」，由此形成英语前缀 poly-，见于 polyglot、polygamy。

items.en: Greek gonia meant 「angle, corner」, from the same root as gony 「knee」.
items.cn: 希腊语 gonia 意为「角、拐角」，与 gony「膝」同源。

items.en: The adjective polugonos meant 「many-angled」; later writers used polygonon for the figure itself.
items.cn: 形容词 polugonos 意为「多角的」；后来的作者用 polygonon 指这种图形本身。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek form as polygonum, keeping it as a bookish geometrical term.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词形作 polygonum，保留为书面几何术语。

items.en: English learned use is recorded in the sixteenth century, when geometry texts revived Greek vocabulary.
items.cn: 英语的书面用法见于十六世纪，当时几何教材大量复兴希腊词汇。

items.en: The word now covers regular and irregular figures, computer boundaries, and test regions alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词既指正与不规则图形，也指电脑边界与检验区域。

note.en: The look-alike group collects Greek and Latin words built on the 「many」 prefix or the 「corner」 root; the near-meaning group collects the neighbouring shapes.
note.cn: 形近组收以「多」前缀或「角」词根构成的希腊、拉丁词；近义组收相邻的平面图形词。

entries.definition: a Greek prefix meaning many, as in polygon and polyglot
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语前缀，意为「多」，见于 polygon 与 polyglot

entries.definition: the Greek word for angle or corner, the source of -gon
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「角、拐角」，是 -gon 的来源

entries.definition: a six-sided plane figure
entries.definitionCN: 六边形

entries.definition: an expression with several terms; only the prefix is shared
entries.definitionCN: 多项式；只是前缀相同，词根不同

entries.definition: a three-sided polygon
entries.definitionCN: 由三条边构成的多边形，即三角形

entries.definition: a four-sided flat figure with straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 由四条直线边构成的四边形

entries.definition: a round figure with a curved edge and no straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 没有直线边、只有一条曲线的圆

entries.definition: the branch of mathematics that studies shapes such as polygons
entries.definitionCN: 研究多边形等图形的数学分支

normalIntro.en: Polygon is built from two transparent Greek parts, so the meaning can be read straight off its spelling.
normalIntro.cn: polygon 由两个意思透明的希腊词素构成，看拼写就能读出意思。

normal.en: Poly- means many, as in polyglot and polygamy.
normal.cn: poly- 意为「多」，见于 polyglot、polygamy。

normal.en: Gonia means corner, so -gon appears in hexagon and octagon.
normal.cn: gonia 意为「角」，所以 -gon 出现于 hexagon、octagon。

normal.en: Tri means three, so a triangle is a three-cornered shape rather than a polygon with few sides.
normal.cn: tri 意为「三」，所以三角形就是「三个角」的形状，而不是边数很少的多边形。

normal.en: The adjective is polygonal, with -al replacing the noun ending.
normal.cn: 形容词是 polygonal，用 -al 替换名词词尾。

normal.en: A regular polygon keeps every side and every angle equal.
normal.cn: regular polygon 是每条边、每个角都相等的多边形。

abstract.en: Picture a piece of string folded into sharp bends and tied closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被折出许多尖角，再首尾系紧。

abstract.en: Think of a pencil walking in straight steps, then coming back to its start.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔一步一步直线走，又走回出发点。

abstract.en: Imagine a plot of land fenced with straight panels.
abstract.cn: 想象一块地用一块块直板围成栅栏。

examples.en: The children cut polygons out of coloured paper.
examples.cn: 孩子们在彩纸上剪出各种多边形。

examples.en: A regular polygon has all sides and all angles equal.
examples.cn: 正多边形的所有边和所有角都相等。

examples.en: The map tool stores each field as a polygon.
examples.cn: 地图工具把每块田地存成一个多边形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破了根」——一把破了的根子由很多小节相连，一节就是一个角，连成一圈就是多边形；这只是谐音拆词，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 poly-（多）+ gonia（角）→ polugonos（多角的）→ 拉丁语 polygonum → 英语 polygon，字面义「多角形」。

sensesIntro.en: Polygon starts as a closed straight-sided figure, narrows to the regular case in geometry, and widens to any many-sided boundary in maps and software.
sensesIntro.cn: polygon 先指直线边围成的封闭图形，再在几何中收窄为正多边形，最后在地图与软件中放宽为任意多边边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed line made of straight segments, with a corner at every bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段段直线连成的封闭折线，每个转折处都有一个角。

branches.en: The general closed figure is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一般的封闭图形是日常义项。

branches.en: The regular case is the geometry sense.
branches.cn: 正多边形是几何义项。

branches.en: A map or screen boundary belongs to working jargon.
branches.cn: 地图或屏幕边界属于工作用语。

branches.en: A closed outline always encloses an inside.
branches.cn: 封闭的轮廓总是围出一块内部。

branches.en: Both senses keep the straight-edged outline but loosen the regularity.
branches.cn: 两者都保留直线轮廓，却放松了规则性。

intro.en: Polygon keeps two Greek parts intact and adds no English suffix of its own.
intro.cn: polygon 完整保留两个希腊词素，本身没有附加英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek compound passed through Latin unchanged in meaning, and Latin supplies the learned -um form polygonum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个希腊复合词经拉丁语传入，意义未变；拉丁语提供了书面的 polygonum 形式。

items.example: Poly- marks the many sides of the figure.
items.exampleCN: poly- 标出图形的「多条边」。

items.example: Gonia is the corner root of the word.
items.exampleCN: gonia 是这个词的「角」词根。

items.example: The Greek noun names the figure directly.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语名词直接为这种图形命名。

items.example: Latin kept the Greek meaning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了希腊语含义。

items.example: The ending -gon marks other figures too.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -gon 也标记其他图形。

items.example: The suffix -al forms polygonal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 polygonal。

items.example: The noun extends the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词进一步扩展词族。

items.example: An irregular polygon has unequal sides.
items.exampleCN: 不规则多边形的边不相等。

items.example: A regular polygon has equal sides.
items.exampleCN: 正多边形的边相等。

definition_zh: 聚合物；高分子化合物；（化学）由许多单体连接而成的大分子；塑料材料
definition_en: a very large molecule made of many small identical units joined in a chain
core_image: 一长串珠子，每颗珠子都是同一个小单元，被反复穿在一起
scene: 工厂里，技术人员把一种乳白色的小颗粒倒进模具，加热后就变成坚硬的塑料外壳。The engineers melted the polymer beads and molded them into a stiff casing.
sceneCN: 这里 polymer 是「聚合物、高分子」（第 1 个义项：由许多重复小单元连接而成的大分子）；句意：工程师把聚合物颗粒熔化，压模成坚硬的外壳。

pos.zh: 聚合物的；高分子材料的

derivatives.zh: 由 polymer 加后缀 -ic 构成，义为「聚合的、高分子的」
由 polymer 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使聚合」
polymerize 的名词形式，义为「聚合作用」
前缀 co-（共同）加 polymer，义为「共聚物」

senses.title: A large molecule built from repeating units
senses.definition: a molecule of very high mass made when many small units called monomers link into long chains
senses.definitionCN: 由许多叫做单体的重复小单元连接成长链后形成的大质量分子
senses.example: Starch is a natural polymer of glucose.
senses.exampleCN: 淀粉是葡萄糖的天然聚合物。
senses.why: Greek poly- means many and meros means part, so a polymer is literally a substance of many parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poly- 意为「多」，meros 意为「部分」，所以 polymer 字面就是「由许多部分组成的物质」。

senses.title: A commercial plastic material
senses.definition: a manufactured material such as nylon or polyethylene that consists mostly of long synthetic molecules
senses.definitionCN: 尼龙、聚乙烯等以长链合成分子为主的工业材料
senses.example: Nylon was the first widely used synthetic polymer.
senses.exampleCN: 尼龙是第一种被广泛使用的合成聚合物。
senses.why: The abstract molecule name moved into shops and factories, where it simply means the plastic you can shape.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的分子名称走进了商店与工厂，在那里它就指可以塑形的塑料。

senses.title: A modelled structure in chemistry
senses.definition: a structure studied or represented with chains and branching, as in a polymer model for teaching or research
senses.definitionCN: 在教学或研究中用链状、支链结构来描绘的分子模型
senses.example: Students built a polymer model from paper loops.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们用纸环搭了一个聚合物模型。
senses.why: Once the molecule is drawn as a chain, the drawing itself becomes a familiar teaching object also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦分子被画成链条，这张图本身也成了同样叫这个名字的常见教学物件。

senses.title: A thing built from many parts
senses.titleCN: 由许多部分组成的东西
senses.definition: figuratively, an ornate poem or a thing composed of many parts, following the literal sense of many parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：多段组成的繁复诗作或由许多构件拼成的事物，源出「许多部分」的字面义
senses.example: The old critic called the epic a verbal polymer.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老批评家称这部史诗为语言的聚合体。
senses.why: The literal image of many parts reappears in figurative writing, where anything pieced together from many bits can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 「许多部分」的字面意象在比喻中重现，凡由许多小块拼合而成之物都可以借用这个名字。

intro.en: Polymer is a nineteenth-century scientific coinage in Swedish from Greek parts, later settled in English.
intro.cn: polymer 是十九世纪在瑞典语中从希腊词素构成的科学新词，后来在英语中定型。

items.en: Greek polus meant 「much, many」 and supplies the poly- seen across scientific vocabulary.
items.cn: 希腊语 polus 意为「多」，提供科学词汇中常见的 poly-。

items.en: Greek meros meant 「part」, which also underlies merism and the scientist term monomer.
items.cn: 希腊语 meros 意为「部分」，也构成 merism 与科学术语 monomer。

items.en: Jons Jacob Berzelius is generally credited with coining the word polymer from the Greek parts in the 1830s, in a sense close to 「different compounds with the same proportions」.
items.cn: 一般认为聚合物一词由永斯·雅各布·贝采利乌斯在十九世纪三十年代用希腊词素造出，原义接近「组成比例相同而性质不同的化合物」。

items.en: English took the word through Latinized scientific usage, first in organic chemistry.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁化的科学用法借入该词，最早用于有机化学。

items.en: Staudinger and his team produced macromolecule work in the 1920s fixed the modern sense of long chains of repeating units.
items.cn: 二十世纪二十年代施陶丁格的高分子研究确立了「重复单元长链」的现代含义。

items.en: The plastics industry spread the word from laboratories to shops, where polymer now means plastic material.
items.cn: 塑料工业把这个词从实验室带进商店，如今 polymer 常指塑料材料。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds sharing the 「many parts」 prefix or the 「part」 root; the near-meaning group collects chemical and material neighbours.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「多」前缀或「部分」词根的合成词；近义组收化学与材料方面的近邻词。

entries.definition: the single small unit that repeats in a polymer
entries.definitionCN: 聚合物中重复出现的小单元

entries.definition: a Greek prefix meaning many, as in polygamy and polygon
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语前缀，意为「多」，见于 polygamy、polygon

entries.definition: the Greek word for part, source of the -mer unit
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「部分」，-mer 的来源

entries.definition: a many-sided flat figure; only the prefix is shared
entries.definitionCN: 多边形；只是前缀相同，词根不同

entries.definition: any very large molecule, including but not limited to polymers
entries.definitionCN: 泛指极大的分子，包括但不限于聚合物

entries.definition: a manufactured material that can be moulded when soft
entries.definitionCN: 可在柔软时塑形的工业材料

entries.definition: made by chemical process rather than grown; polymers are often this
entries.definitionCN: 由化学方法制成而非天然生长的，聚合物常属此类

entries.definition: a substance of two or more elements chemically joined
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或多种元素化合而成的物质

normalIntro.en: Polymer is a clean two-part Greek word: many plus part, with the rest of the family built on -mer.
normalIntro.cn: polymer 由两个清晰的希腊词素构成：多 + 部分，词族其余成员都以 -mer 为核心。

normal.en: Poly- means many, as in polygon and polyglot.
normal.cn: poly- 意为「多」，见于 polygon、polyglot。

normal.en: -Mer means part, so monomer is the single part and polymer the many-part chain.
normal.cn: -mer 意为「部分」，所以 monomer 是单个部分，polymer 是多部分长链。

normal.en: The adjective polymeric and the verb polymerize both keep the same stem.
normal.cn: 形容词 polymeric 与动词 polymerize 都保留同一个词干。

normal.en: Polymerization names the act of linking units together.
normal.cn: polymerization 指把单元连接起来的过程。

normal.en: The plastics industry shortened the word in speech to plain plastic, but polymer stays the technical name.
normal.cn: 塑料行业在日常口语中把它简称为 plastic，但 polymer 仍是技术名称。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace where every bead is identical.
abstract.cn: 想象一串每个珠子都一模一样的项链。

abstract.en: Think of a paper chain cut from one repeated loop.
abstract.cn: 想象用同一个纸环反复剪接成的纸链。

abstract.en: Imagine a long train of identical boxcars.
abstract.cn: 想象一列由相同车厢连成的长火车。

examples.en: Cellulose is a polymer found in the walls of plant cells.
examples.cn: 纤维素是存在于植物细胞壁中的一种聚合物。

examples.en: The new material is a polymer that conducts electricity.
examples.cn: 这种新材料是一种能导电的聚合物。

examples.en: Chemists link small monomers into long chains during polymerization.
examples.cn: 化学家在聚合过程中把小分子单体连成长链。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波兰摸」——波兰人摸着一长串珠子，珠子一颗颗连成长链，就是聚合物；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 poly-（多）+ meros（部分）→ 十九世纪瑞典化学家以希腊词素造词 polymer，字面义「许多部分组成的物质」，现代义指重复单元长链。

sensesIntro.en: Polymer moves from a molecule of many repeating parts to the plastic made of such molecules, to a teaching model, to a figurative many-part thing.
sensesIntro.cn: polymer 从「由许多重复部分组成的分子」，走到由这种分子制成的塑料材料，再到教学模型，最后到比喻性的「多部分组成之物」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long chain of identical beads, each bead one small part.
core.cn: 核心意象：一长串相同的珠子，每颗珠子就是一个小的部分。

branches.en: The many-part molecule is the core scientific sense.
branches.cn: 多部分大分子是核心科学义项。

branches.en: The plastic material is the shop-floor sense.
branches.cn: 塑料材料是车间义项。

branches.en: The drawn model is the teaching sense.
branches.cn: 画出的模型是教学义项。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the image of many parts joined together.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在「许多部分连在一起」的意象上。

branches.en: Material and model share the visible chain structure.
branches.cn: 材料与模型共享可见的链状结构。

intro.en: Polymer is Greek poly- plus Greek -mer, and English adds standard suffixes such as -ic and -ize.
intro.cn: polymer 是希腊前缀 poly- 加希腊词素 -mer，英语再附加 -ic、-ize 等标准后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Greek parts reached English through Latinized scientific writing, so Latin supplies no independent root of its own here.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词素经拉丁化的科学写作进入英语，拉丁语在这里没有独立的词根。

items.example: Poly- marks the many repeating units.
items.exampleCN: poly- 标出「许多重复单元」。

items.example: Meros is the part root of the word.
items.exampleCN: meros 是这个词的「部分」词根。

items.example: The ending -mer appears in monomer and dimer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -mer 见于 monomer、dimer。

items.example: Monomer means one part.
items.exampleCN: monomer 意为「一个部分」。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms polymeric.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 polymeric。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms polymerize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 polymerize。

items.example: The suffix -ization forms polymerization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ization 构成 polymerization。

items.example: Co- plus polymer gives copolymer.
items.exampleCN: co- 加 polymer 得到 copolymer。

items.example: Macro- plus molecule gives macromolecule.
items.exampleCN: macro- 加 molecule 得到 macromolecule。

definition_zh: 聚合作用；（分子）聚合
definition_en: a chemical process in which many small molecules join together to form one very large molecule
core_image: 成千上万个小纸扣一节一节扣成一条长链
scene: 塑料厂里，工人们把反应釜的温度调到恰到好处，让原料小分子连成长链。In the plastics plant the workers kept the reactor at just the right temperature so that the small molecules could begin polymerization.
sceneCN: 这里 polymerization 是「聚合作用」（第 1 个义项：小分子连成大分子的化学过程）；句意：塑料厂里，工人们把反应釜的温度调到恰到好处，让原料小分子连成长链。

derivatives.zh: 由 polymer 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使聚合」
基础词，义为「聚合物、高分子」
由 polymer 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「聚合物的」
加前缀 de- 表示反向过程，义为「解聚作用」

senses.title: The joining of small molecules into long chains
senses.definition: the chemical process by which many small molecules link together to form long, heavy molecules
senses.definitionCN: 许多小分子连接起来形成长而重的分子的化学过程
senses.example: Polymerization turns simple gases and liquids into solid plastics.
senses.exampleCN: 聚合作用把简单的气体和液体变成固体塑料。
senses.why: The Greek root poly- means many and -mer means part, so the word names the act of joining many parts into one chain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 poly- 意为「多」，-mer 意为「部分」，所以这个词指把许多部分连成一条链的动作。

senses.title: A method used in industry
senses.definition: the industrial method of making synthetic materials such as plastics, fibres, and rubbers by linking monomers
senses.definitionCN: 在工厂里通过连接单体来制造塑料、纤维和橡胶等合成材料的工艺方法
senses.example: The factory uses catalytic polymerization to make strong bottles.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂用催化聚合的方法制造结实的瓶子。
senses.why: Once chemists learned to control the link-up in reactors, the natural idea became a large-scale industrial technique.
senses.whyCN: 化学家学会在反应釜里控制这种连接之后，这个原本的概念就变成了大规模的工业技术。

senses.title: The state of being linked into a polymer
senses.definition: the condition or extent to which molecules have been joined into larger polymer chains
senses.definitionCN: 分子已被连接成大聚合链的状态或程度
senses.example: Too much heat can stop the material from reaching full polymerization.
senses.exampleCN: 温度过高会让材料无法达到完全聚合的状态。
senses.why: The process noun also names its result, so we can speak of how far the link-up has gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示过程的名词也用来指结果，所以可以说连接进行到了什么程度。

intro.en: Polymerization combines the Greek elements poly- (many), -mer (part), and the chemical suffix -ization (process).
intro.cn: polymerization 由希腊语成分 poly-（多）、-mer（部分）和化学后缀 -ization（过程）组合而成。

items.en: Greek polys means many, and meros means a part.
items.cn: 希腊语 polys 意为多，meros 意为部分。

items.en: Polymeros means having many parts.
items.cn: polymeros 意为「有许多部分」。

items.en: Berzelius adopts the term polymer for substances with the same makeup but heavier molecules.
items.cn: 化学家贝采利乌斯采用 polymer 一词，指成分相同但分子更重的物质。

items.en: Polymerize appears, meaning to combine into a larger molecule.
items.cn: 英语出现 polymerize，表示聚合成更大的分子。

items.en: The plastics industry turns polymerization into a familiar technical term.
items.cn: 塑料工业让 polymerization 成为日常见到的技术术语。

note.en: Polymerization belongs to the polymer word family and sits beside processes such as condensation and catalysis.
note.cn: polymerization 属于 polymer 词族，并与 condensation、catalysis 等过程词相邻。

entries.definition: a large molecule built from many small units
entries.definitionCN: 由许多小单元构成的大分子；聚合物

entries.definition: to combine into a polymer
entries.definitionCN: 聚合；使聚合成高分子

entries.definition: made of or relating to polymers
entries.definitionCN: 聚合物的；高分子的

entries.definition: a synthetic fibre made from polymers
entries.definitionCN: 由聚合物制成的合成纤维；涤纶

entries.definition: a reaction in which small molecules join and a small by-product is lost
entries.definitionCN: 缩合反应，小分子结合并失去一个小分子副产物

entries.definition: the speeding up of a reaction by a substance that is not used up
entries.definitionCN: 催化剂加速反应而自身不被消耗的作用

entries.definition: the building of a complex substance from simpler ones
entries.definitionCN: 由简单物质合成复杂物质

normalIntro.en: Polymerization is the word family of poly-, -mer, and the process suffix -ization.
normalIntro.cn: polymerization 由 poly-、-mer 与过程后缀 -ization 组成。

normal.en: The prefix poly- means many, as in polygon or polysyllabic.
normal.cn: 前缀 poly- 意为「多」，如 polygon（多边形）与多音节词。

normal.en: The element -mer means part, so a polymer is a substance of many parts.
normal.cn: 成分 -mer 意为「部分」，所以 polymer 就是「由许多部分」构成的物质。

normal.en: The suffix -ization marks a process, so polymerization is the act of becoming a polymer.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ization 表示过程，因此 polymerization 就是「变成聚合物」的过程。

normal.en: Addition polymerization simply adds monomers; condensation polymerization loses a small molecule as it joins.
normal.cn: 加聚反应只是把单体接连起来；缩聚反应在连接时会失去一个小分子。

normal.en: The degree of polymerization tells you how many units are linked in one chain.
normal.cn: 「聚合度」告诉你一条链里连了多少个单元。

abstract.en: Picture thousands of paper clips clicking into one endless chain.
abstract.cn: 想象成千上万个小纸扣一个接一个扣成一条无尽的长链。

abstract.en: Imagine a factory where tiny white balls roll into a machine and come out as clear plastic bottles.
abstract.cn: 想象小小白球滚进一台机器，出来时变成透明的塑料瓶。

abstract.en: Think of a half-finished necklace: the link-up has begun but is not yet complete.
abstract.cn: 想象一串还没串完的项链：连接已经开始，却还没有完成。

examples.en: Polymerization is the basic reaction behind most modern plastics.
examples.cn: 聚合作用是大多数现代塑料背后的基本反应。

examples.en: Control of temperature is essential during polymerization.
examples.cn: 聚合过程中控制温度至关重要。

examples.en: Naturally occurring silk is the product of a slow biological polymerization.
examples.cn: 天然丝绸是一种缓慢的生物聚合过程的产物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「跑了来买」——小分子跑过来一个挨一个，慢慢「买」成一条长链；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语词素 poly-（多）+ meros（部分）→ 希腊语 polymeros（有许多部分）→ 拉丁术语 polymer（聚合物）→ 英语 polymer + 动词后缀 -ize + 过程后缀 -ation → polymerization，核心义「许多部分连成一体」。

sensesIntro.en: Polymerization starts as the chemical act of joining many small molecules, grows into an industrial method, and finally names the state reached by that process.
sensesIntro.cn: polymerization 先指许多小分子连接起来的化学动作，再指工业上的制造工艺，最后指这个过程达到的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: countless small links forming one long chain.
core.cn: 核心意象：无数个小环节扣成一条长链。

branches.en: The chemical link-up is the core sense.
branches.cn: 化学层面的连接是核心义项。

branches.en: The factory method grows out of the core reaction.
branches.cn: 工厂里的工艺方法由核心反应发展而来。

branches.en: The process also names how far the link-up has gone.
branches.cn: 这个过程名词也指连接进行到的状态。

branches.en: A reaction in a flask and a method in a plant are the same process at different scales.
branches.cn: 烧瓶里的反应与工厂里的工艺是同一过程的不同规模。

branches.en: Industry controls the temperature so that the material reaches full polymerization.
branches.cn: 工厂控制温度，好让材料达到完全聚合的状态。

intro.en: Polymerization is a three-part build: the Greek prefix poly-, the root -mer, and the process suffix -ization.
intro.cn: polymerization 由三部分构成：希腊前缀 poly-、词根 -mer 与过程后缀 -ization。

latinIntro.en: The building blocks are Greek, while the scientific term polymer was coined in Latin style in the 1830s.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的构件来自希腊语，而科学术语 polymer 在十九世纪三十年代按拉丁语的方式被造出。

items.example: The prefix poly- appears in polygon and polymer.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 poly- 出现在 polygon 与 polymer 中。

items.example: The root -mer marks a single repeated unit.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -mer 表示一个重复的单元。

items.example: The suffix -ize turns polymer into polymerize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 把 polymer 变成 polymerize。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms polymerization from polymerize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 由 polymerize 构成 polymerization。

items.meaning: a small molecule that can join into a chain
items.meaningCN: 可连成长链的小分子；单体
items.example: Monomers are the units that start polymerization.
items.exampleCN: 单体是启动聚合的单元。

items.meaning: the breaking of a polymer back into units
items.example: Heat can cause depolymerization of some plastics.
items.exampleCN: 高温会使某些塑料发生解聚。

items.example: Polymeric fibres are used in sports clothing.
items.exampleCN: 聚合物纤维用于运动服装。

items.meaning: a polymer fibre used in clothing
items.example: Polyester is produced by polymerization.
items.exampleCN: 涤纶是经聚合制成的。

latinEntries.meaning: a compound with many repeating parts

definition_zh: 息肉；水螅体
definition_en: a small growth on the inside of the body, or a tiny sea animal with a tube-shaped body and a ring of tentacles
core_image: 礁石上一个圆口伸出许多细触手的小动物
scene: 医生做肠镜检查时，在肠壁上发现了一个小突起，取样送去化验。During the colonoscopy the doctor found a small polyp on the wall of the intestine and sent a sample to the lab.
sceneCN: 这里 polyp 是「息肉」（第 1 个义项：体内黏膜上长出的小突起）；句意：医生做肠镜检查时，在肠壁上发现了一个小突起，取样送去化验。

derivatives.zh: 由 polyp 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「息肉状的」
polyp 与希腊语 ektome（切除）组合，义为「息肉切除术」
另含 poly-（多）成分，义为「多倍体的」，与息肉义无关

senses.title: A growth inside the body
senses.definition: a small lump that grows from the inner lining of the nose, intestine, or another hollow organ
senses.definitionCN: 从鼻子、肠道或其他中空器官内壁长出的肉质小突起
senses.example: A routine screening found a small polyp in her colon.
senses.exampleCN: 一次常规筛查在她的结肠里发现了一个小息肉。
senses.why: Doctors borrowed the name of the many-footed sea animal for flesh-like growths that hang like little bodies.
senses.whyCN: 医生借用了「多足小动物」的名字，来形容那些像小身体一样垂挂的肉质突起。

senses.title: A simple sea animal
senses.definition: a simple water animal with a tube-shaped body, a mouth ringed by tentacles, and a base fixed to rock or shell
senses.definitionCN: 身体呈管状、口部环生触手、基部附着在岩石或贝壳上的简单水生动物
senses.example: Each coral reef is built by millions of tiny polyps.
senses.exampleCN: 每片珊瑚礁都由数百万个微小的珊瑚虫建造而成。
senses.why: The Greek root literally means many-footed, and the ring of tentacles gives the animal its many feet.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根本义是「多足的」，而它环生的触手正是那些「许多脚」。

senses.title: The animal in its fixed stage
senses.definition: the attached form of a jellyfish or related animal, in contrast to the swimming stage it may also have
senses.definitionCN: 与水母或其他相关动物可自由游动的阶段相对、固定不动的形态
senses.example: The jellyfish alternates between a swimming stage and a stationary polyp.
senses.exampleCN: 水母在游动阶段与固着不动的水螅体之间交替。
senses.why: In its life cycle the animal appears first as a fixed polyp, so the word also names that stage.
senses.whyCN: 在这种动物的生活史里，它先以固定不动的水螅体出现，于是这个词也用来指这个阶段。

intro.en: Polyp comes through Latin from Greek polypous, literally many-footed, and was first used for the tentacled sea creature.
intro.cn: polyp 经拉丁语来自希腊语 polypous，字面意思是「多足的」，最初用来指带触手的海洋生物。

items.en: Greek polys (many) and pous (foot) combine as polypous, the octopus.
items.cn: 希腊语 polys（多）与 pous（脚）组合成 polypous，指章鱼。

items.en: Latin polypus borrows the Greek word and later includes the sea polyp.
items.cn: 拉丁语 polypus 借入该希腊词，后来也涵盖海生水螅体。

items.en: The same Latin word names a growth in the nose, called a polypus like a small body.
items.cn: 同一拉丁词也用来指鼻内的增生物，被称为「像小身体一样」的息肉。

items.en: The word is first recorded in English in medical writing and as the name of the sea animal.
items.cn: 该词在英语中最早见于医学文献，也用作这种海洋动物的名称。

items.en: Modern medicine applies it to growths in the colon and other organs.
items.cn: 现代医学把这些叫法扩展到结肠及其他器官的增生物。

note.en: Polyp shares the Greek poly- element with many science words and stands close to medical and marine terms.
note.cn: polyp 与许多科学词汇共享希腊语成分 poly-，并与医学、海洋生物学术语相邻。

entries.definition: a prefix meaning many
entries.definitionCN: 表示「多」的前缀

entries.definition: having more than two sets of chromosomes
entries.definitionCN: 多倍体的，染色体多于两套的

entries.definition: a common plastic made of long linked molecules
entries.definitionCN: 一种常见的塑料，由长链分子构成

entries.definition: a survey of opinions
entries.definitionCN: 民意调查；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small hard growth on the skin
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤上的小疣，长在体表而非内壁

entries.definition: a small rounded lump in the body or on a plant
entries.definitionCN: 身体或植物上的小结节

entries.definition: a long thin arm used by a sea animal for touch or catching food
entries.definitionCN: 海洋动物用来触探或捕食的长触手

entries.definition: a hard rock-like substance built by colonies of tiny sea polyps
entries.definitionCN: 由细小珊瑚虫群体形成的坚硬珊瑚

normalIntro.en: Polyp is a Greek build of poly- (many) and pous (foot), later stretched to medical growths.
normalIntro.cn: polyp 由希腊语 poly-（多）与 pous（脚）构成，后来延伸到医学上的增生物。

normal.en: The prefix poly- means many, and the same prefix appears in polygon.
normal.cn: 前缀 poly- 意为「多」，polygon（多边形）用的也是这个前缀。

normal.en: The second half comes from Greek pous, a foot, seen also in tripod.
normal.cn: 后半部分来自希腊语 pous（脚），tripod（三脚架）里也有相似成分。

normal.en: A polyp began as a many-footed sea creature, which is why it now names tentacled animals.
normal.cn: polyp 最初指「多足的」海洋生物，所以现在用来指带触手的动物。

normal.en: Medicine borrowed the image for small growths that hang from a lining.
normal.cn: 医学借用了这个形象，指从黏膜上垂下来的小突起。

normal.en: Do not confuse polyp with poll: one is a growth, the other is a survey or a vote.
normal.cn: 不要把 polyp 和 poll 混用：前者是增生物，后者是民调或投票。

abstract.en: Picture a rock covered with tiny open mouths, each waving a crown of thread-like arms.
abstract.cn: 想象礁石上布满小小的圆口，每一口都摇着一圈线一样的细臂。

abstract.en: Imagine a mushroom growing out of the soft lining of a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蘑菇从柔软的内壁里冒出来。

abstract.en: Think of a jellyfish standing still on its head, fixed to the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水母倒立着停在海底，一动不动。

examples.en: Most polyps are harmless, but some can turn into cancer.
examples.cn: 大多数息肉是无害的，但有些可能转变为癌症。

examples.en: Each polyp has a mouth surrounded by stinging tentacles.
examples.cn: 每个水螅体都有一个被蛰刺触手环绕的口。

examples.en: The doctor removed two polyps during the examination.
examples.cn: 医生在检查中切除了两个息肉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡立」——长在肠壁上像小坡一样凸起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 polys（多）+ pous（脚）→ 希腊语 polypous（多足的，指章鱼）→ 拉丁语 polypus（亦指鼻内增生物）→ 英语 polyp，核心义「多足的小身体」。

sensesIntro.en: Polyp begins with the medical growth, extends to the tentacled sea animal, and finally names the fixed stage of that animal.
sensesIntro.cn: polyp 先指医学上的增生物，再指带触手的海洋动物，最后指这种动物固着的阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body with many feet waving from a rock.
core.cn: 核心意象：礁石上伸出一副带着许多小脚的细长身体。

branches.en: The lump inside the body is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 体内长出的肉块是医学义项。

branches.en: The tentacled sea animal is the original sense.
branches.cn: 带触手的海生动物是本义。

branches.en: The fixed life stage grows from the same body shape.
branches.cn: 固着的生命周期阶段由同一种身体形态发展而来。

branches.en: Both the growth and the animal are small bodies attached to a surface.
branches.cn: 增生物与这种动物都是附着在表面的小身体。

branches.en: Colonies of polyps build the coral that shelters many fish.
branches.cn: 珊瑚虫群体建造的珊瑚礁为许多鱼类提供栖息地。

intro.en: Polyp joins the Greek prefix poly- to a root for foot, with several English and medical compounds built around it.
intro.cn: polyp 由希腊前缀 poly- 与表示「脚」的词根组合而成，并衍生出若干英语与医学复合词。

latinIntro.en: Greek polypous passed into Latin as polypus and then into English, retaining both the sea animal and the nasal growth.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 polypous 进入拉丁语成为 polypus，再进入英语，同时保留海生动物与鼻内增生物两义。

items.example: The prefix poly- marks words meaning many parts.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 poly- 出现在表示「许多部分」的词里。

items.example: The root pous appears in podiatry and tripod.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pous 见于 podiatry 与 tripod。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms polypous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 polypous。

items.example: Polyps are common in the colon.
items.exampleCN: 息肉常见于结肠。

items.example: The suffix -ectomy joins polyp in polypectomy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ectomy 与 polyp 组合成 polypectomy。

items.example: A polypectomy takes only a few minutes.
items.exampleCN: 息肉切除术只需几分钟。

items.example: Polypous tissue was sent for testing.
items.exampleCN: 息肉状组织被送去检验。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms words for shapes that resemble something.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -oid 构成表示「形状相似」的形容词。

latinEntries.meaning: the many-footed sea creature, an octopus
octopus, sea polyp, or nasal growth
latinEntries.meaningCN: 章鱼、海生水螅体或鼻内增生物

definition_zh: 沉思；考虑；琢磨
definition_en: to think about something carefully for a long time, especially before making a decision
core_image: 一个人托着腮，把一件事放在手里反复掂量
scene: 深夜，他托着腮坐在书桌前，反复琢磨该不该接受那份工作。Late at night he sat at his desk, chin on his hand, and began to ponder whether he should accept the job.
sceneCN: 这里 ponder 是「沉思、反复琢磨」（第 1 个义项：长时间认真地想一件事）；句意：深夜，他托着腮坐在书桌前，反复琢磨该不该接受那份工作。

derivatives.zh: 与 ponder 同源于拉丁语 ponderare（称量），义为「笨重的；沉闷的」
由 ponder 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「重量；重要性」，多用于 preponderance
由 ponder 加 -ing 构成，义为「深思；思索」

senses.title: To think about something carefully
senses.definition: to think carefully and at length about a question or a possible action
senses.definitionCN: 对一个疑问或可能的行动进行长时间认真的思考
senses.example: She pondered the offer for several days before replying.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这份工作机会琢磨了好几天才回信。
senses.why: The Latin source means to weigh, so pondering is the mind turning a matter over and over like a heavy object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「称量」，所以沉思就是把一件事像重物一样在心头反复掂量。

senses.title: To wonder reflectively
senses.definition: to wonder quietly about something, especially in the form of a question or a choice
senses.definitionCN: 安静地琢磨某事，常带出一个疑问或选择
senses.example: He pondered what the letter might mean.
senses.exampleCN: 他琢磨这封信究竟是什么意思。
senses.why: When the object is a question, the weighing becomes a slow turning over of possibilities in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是一个问题时，这种「掂量」就变成在心里慢慢翻转各种可能性。

senses.title: To think deeply without speaking
senses.definition: to give long, quiet thought to a serious subject, usually without speaking
senses.definitionCN: 对严肃的话题进行长时间的静默思考，通常不开口
senses.example: The old man sat by the fire and pondered.
senses.exampleCN: 老人坐在炉火旁沉思。
senses.why: Used without an object, the verb names the silent act of weighing things in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 不带宾语使用时，这个动词指的是在心里默默掂量的动作。

intro.en: Ponder comes from Latin ponderare, to weigh, which comes from pondus, a weight.
intro.cn: ponder 来自拉丁语 ponderare（称量），而 ponderare 又来自 pondus（重量）。

items.en: Pondus means weight, and ponderare means to weigh or estimate.
items.cn: pondus 意为重量，ponderare 意为称量或估量。

items.en: Writers use ponderare for weighing reasons and judgment, not just goods.
items.cn: 中世纪作家把 ponderare 用于权衡理由与作出判断，而不只是称货。

items.en: Ponderer carries the weighing sense into French.
items.cn: ponderer 把「称量」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Ponder is first recorded in English with the meaning to weigh mentally.
items.cn: ponder 在英语中最早见于十四世纪，意为「在心里称量」。

items.en: The literal weighing fades, leaving the everyday sense of thinking carefully.
items.cn: 字面的称量意味逐渐淡去，留下日常所说的「仔细思考」。

note.en: Ponder belongs to a small family of weighing words and sits beside verbs for thinking.
note.cn: ponder 属于一小群表示「称量」的词汇，并与表示思考的一类动词相邻。

entries.definition: heavy and slow, or dull and serious in style
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；笨拙的；文风沉闷的

entries.definition: a greater weight or number of one thing over another
entries.definitionCN: 优势；占多数

entries.definition: weight or importance
entries.definitionCN: 重量；分量（罕用词）

entries.definition: a unit of weight or money
entries.definitionCN: 磅；英镑；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to think about something seriously for a period of time
entries.definitionCN: 认真思索；考虑

entries.definition: to discuss or think about something carefully, often with others
entries.definitionCN: 仔细考虑；商议

entries.definition: to think quietly about something
entries.definitionCN: 沉思；冥想

normalIntro.en: Ponder is a weighing verb: its Latin root means a weight, and its family includes ponderous and preponderance.
normalIntro.cn: ponder 本义与「称量」有关：拉丁词根意为重量，同族词有 ponderous 与 preponderance。

normal.en: The Latin root pondus means weight, so to ponder is to weigh ideas.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 pondus 意为重量，所以 ponder 就是给想法「称重」。

normal.en: Ponderous keeps the physical sense of heavy, while ponder keeps the mental sense of weighing.
normal.cn: ponderous 保留了「沉重」的物理意义，ponder 则保留「掂量」的心智意义。

normal.en: With the particles over or on, the verb often describes slow, unhurried thought.
normal.cn: 与 over 或 on 这类小品词搭配时，常指缓慢、不慌不忙的思考。

normal.en: You can ponder a question, a decision, or a mystery, but not usually a person.
normal.cn: 可以说 ponder 一个问题、决定或谜团，但一般不说对某人 ponder。

normal.en: Compare with think over: think over is more everyday, ponder is slightly formal and heavier.
normal.cn: 对比 think over（仔细想想）：后者更日常，ponder 稍正式，分量也更重。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar holding a stone in each hand and steadily comparing their weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者两手各握一块石头，稳稳地比较它们的轻重。

abstract.en: Imagine a question floating above your head, turning slowly like a slow wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题浮在头顶，像慢轮一样缓缓翻转。

abstract.en: See an old man by the fire, hands folded, eyes half closed, saying nothing at all.
abstract.cn: 设想炉火旁的老人双手交叠，半闭着眼，一言不发。

examples.en: Scientists still ponder why the ice sheets retreated so quickly.
examples.cn: 科学家仍在琢磨冰盖为何消退得那样快。

examples.en: He pondered over the decision for weeks.
examples.cn: 他为这个决定斟酌了好几个星期。

examples.en: She pondered whether to tell the truth.
examples.cn: 她琢磨着要不要说实话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「畔的」——一个人沿着河边慢慢踱步，心里盘算事情；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pondus（重量）→ 拉丁语 ponderare（称量、估量）→ 古法语 ponderer → 英语 ponder，核心义「把事物放在心里称量」。

sensesIntro.en: Ponder moves from thinking carefully about a choice, through wondering about a question, to silent reflection on a serious subject.
sensesIntro.cn: ponder 由对选择的仔细思考，转为对疑问的琢磨，最后指对严肃话题的静默深思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand weighing a heavy object before deciding.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在决定前掂量一件重物的分量。

branches.en: Careful thinking about a choice is the central sense.
branches.cn: 对选择的仔细思考是中心义项。

branches.en: Wondering about a question turns the weighing into slow questioning.
branches.cn: 对疑问的琢磨使「称量」变成缓慢的追问。

branches.en: Silent reflection keeps only the inward act of weighing.
branches.cn: 静默深思只保留了内在的掂量动作。

branches.en: Deciding and wondering both begin with the same mental balance.
branches.cn: 做决定与琢磨疑问都始于同一种心里的权衡。

branches.en: A long question often ends in wordless, patient thought.
branches.cn: 一个长久悬挂的疑问，往往最后落入无言的耐心思考。

intro.en: Ponder carries the Latin root for weight, and the same root builds ponderous and preponderance.
intro.cn: ponder 带着表示「重量」的拉丁词根，同一词根还构成 ponderous 与 preponderance。

latinIntro.en: Latin pondus is a weight and ponderare is to weigh; the metaphor of weighing became thinking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pondus 是重量，ponderare 是称量；「称量」的比喻由此转为「思考」。

items.example: The root pondus survives in ponder and preponderance.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pondus 保留在 ponder 与 pound 中。

items.example: The ending makes the Latin root into the English verb ponder.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把拉丁词根变成英语动词 ponder。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms ponderous, meaning heavy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 ponderous，意为沉重。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms ponderance from ponder.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 由 ponder 构成 ponderance。

items.example: The prefix pre- creates preponderance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 构成 preponderance。

items.example: Pondering names the act of thinking deeply.
items.exampleCN: pondering 指深思这一行为。

items.example: Ponderable describes something that has weight.
items.exampleCN: ponderable 形容有重量的事物。

items.example: A preponderance of soldiers decided the battle.
items.exampleCN: 士兵数量的优势决定了这场战斗。

definition_zh: 沉重的；笨重的；笨拙迟缓的；沉闷冗长的
definition_en: slow and heavy because of great weight, or dull and laboured in style
core_image: 一尊石像被几个人抬着，每挪一步都重重压在地面上
scene: 搬家公司抬一架老式立式钢琴上楼，三步一停，楼梯板被压得直响。The removal men set the old upright piano on the landing and caught their breath, for it was too ponderous to carry up the last flight without a rest.
sceneCN: 这里 ponderous 是「沉重的、笨重的」（第 1 个义项：因重量大而难以搬动的）；句意：搬家公司把老式立式钢琴放到楼梯口喘口气，因为它太笨重，不歇一歇抬不上最后一段楼梯。

pos.zh: 沉重的；笨重的；笨拙迟缓的；沉闷冗长的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「吃力地；笨拙迟钝地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「笨重；沉闷」
与 ponderous 同源于拉丁语「称重」，义为「沉思、仔细权衡」
由 pre-（在前）+ ponderare（称重）+ -ance 构成，义为「优势；占多数」
由 equi-（相等）+ 拉丁语 poise（重量）构成，义为「平衡；均衡」

senses.title: Very heavy and hard to move
senses.definition: so large and heavy that it is difficult to lift or move
senses.definitionCN: 体积大、分量重，难以抬起或移动
senses.example: The ponderous stone door took four men to open it.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇沉重的石门要四个人才推得开。
senses.why: Latin ponderosus came from pondus, a weight, so the word pictured a thing that hangs heavy on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ponderosus 出自 pondus（重量），原义就是「在秤上沉下去的东西」，所以重量的画面是这个词的本义。

senses.title: Moving slowly and heavily
senses.definition: moving or acting slowly, heavily and with visible effort
senses.definitionCN: 行动缓慢笨重，看得出很费力
senses.example: The ponderous lorry laboured up the hill in second gear.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆笨重的大货车挂着二挡，吃力地爬上山坡。
senses.why: When weight is shown as movement, the scale image turns into a slow, laboured gait.
senses.whyCN: 把重量放进动作里，秤上的画面就变成缓慢吃力的步伐：重的东西动起来自然慢。

senses.title: Awkward and clumsy in manner
senses.definition: awkward, graceless or lacking lightness in behaviour or movement
senses.definitionCN: 举止或动作笨拙、不灵巧、缺乏轻盈感
senses.example: He made a ponderous attempt to thank her, shifting his weight from foot to foot.
senses.exampleCN: 他笨拙地想要道谢，两只脚来回倒着重心。
senses.why: A body weighed down cannot turn quickly, so heaviness becomes a metaphor for social clumsiness.
senses.whyCN: 被重量压住的身体转不过弯，于是「重」就被借来形容人际交往中的笨拙。

senses.title: Dull and laboured in style
senses.definition: too long, slow and dull in speech or writing, so that reading it feels like effort
senses.definitionCN: 言辞或文字过长、缓慢、乏味，读起来像在搬运重物
senses.example: The report is ponderous and full of long introductions instead of clear figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告冗长沉闷，满是长篇序言，却不见清晰的数据。
senses.why: Reading a heavy sentence feels like lifting a heavy object, so weight shifts from the page to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 读一句厚重的话就像举起一件重物，重量于是从纸面转移到了读者脑子里。

senses.title: Large, serious and imposing
senses.definition: large, serious and impressive, especially in a formal or public setting
senses.definitionCN: 规模宏大、庄重肃穆，尤见于正式或公开场合
senses.example: The court met in a ponderous hall lined with marble columns.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭设在一座排着大理石柱的宏伟大厅里。
senses.why: Great weight is also great gravity, so the word can name buildings and ceremonies that press on the visitor.
senses.whyCN: 分量重也意味着气氛庄重，因此这个词也能形容压迫人的建筑与仪式。

senses.title: Slow to act or decide
senses.titleCN: 迟钝拖拉的；官僚繁冗的
senses.definition: slow to respond or decide, often because the organisation carries too much routine
senses.definitionCN: 反应或决断迟缓，常因机构背负了过多程序
senses.example: The ponderous machinery of the ministry took two years to approve the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该部委繁冗迟滞的运作体系用了两年才批准这项计划。
senses.why: An institution that carries weight moves like a loaded cart, so the heavy thing becomes slow procedure.
senses.whyCN: 背负重量的机构像一辆装满货的车，于是「重物」就转化成了层层拖延的程序。

senses.title: Weighing heavily on the mind
senses.definition: felt as a burden or worry that rests heavily on a person
senses.definitionCN: 被感受到的负担或忧虑，压在人心上
senses.example: A ponderous silence filled the room after the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 判决之后，一种沉重的寂静笼罩了整个房间。
senses.why: The original sense is physical weight, and the mind keeps that scale: a worry also has a weight.
senses.whyCN: 本义是物理上的重量，而人心保留了这杆秤：忧虑同样有分量。

senses.title: Massive without grace in shape
senses.definition: big and solid in shape, but without grace or elegance
senses.definitionCN: 体形巨大结实，却缺乏灵动与美感
senses.example: The new civic centre is ponderous and blocks the view of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 新市民中心体量臃肿，挡住了河上的风景。
senses.why: The scale image reaches architecture: what is merely big and solid comes to seem heavy and shapeless.
senses.whyCN: 秤上的画面延伸到建筑：只是又大又实的东西，也会显得沉重而缺少形韵。

intro.en: Ponderous comes from Latin ponderosus, heavy, from pondus, a weight, which is related to pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: ponderous 来自拉丁语 ponderosus（沉重的），出自 pondus（重量），与 pendere（悬挂）同族。

items.en: The reconstructed root means to hang or to weigh, as a thing hangs from a balance.
items.cn: 重构词根表示「悬挂、称量」，如同物品挂在秤上。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or weigh, and pondus names the weight itself.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂、称量，pondus 指重量本身。

items.en: Ponderare means to weigh or ponder, and ponderosus means heavy or weighty.
items.cn: ponderare 意为称重、掂量，ponderare 派生的 ponderosus 意为沉重的、有分量的。

items.en: The adjective stays in scholarly use, describing heavy bodies and solemn texts.
items.cn: 该形容词在中世纪学术拉丁语中沿用，形容沉重的物体与庄重的文本。

items.en: Ponderous enters English as a heavy, weighty adjective, keeping the Latin sense.
items.cn: ponderous 于十五世纪进入英语，沿用拉丁语「沉重、有分量」之义。

items.en: The word spreads from physical weight to slow minds, dull prose and clumsy manners.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从物理重量扩展到迟钝的头脑、沉闷的文笔与笨拙的举止。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root words for hanging and weighing; the near-meaning group gathers the neighbouring words for heavy things and slow motion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「悬挂、称重」词根的词族；近义组收表示沉重、迟缓的近邻词。

entries.definition: to think about something carefully for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「沉思、仔细考虑」，与 ponderous 同出「称量」之义。

entries.definition: in a heavy, slow or laboured way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「吃力地、笨重地、迟缓地」。

entries.definition: the quality of being heavy, slow or dull.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沉重、笨重、沉闷」。

entries.definition: prevailing or greater in number or weight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占优势的、占多数的」，与 pre- 及 ponderare 同源。

entries.definition: having real weight, or worth weighing in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有重量的、值得斟酌的」。

entries.definition: large, heavy and strong, often said of the weight of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指又大又重、分量足，口语色彩更浓。

entries.definition: large and awkward to carry or use, more about clumsiness than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，侧重体积大、搬用不便，比 ponderous 更强调笨拙而非分量。

entries.definition: done with difficulty and not flowing freely, especially of writing or speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，意为「费力的、不流畅的」，多形容文笔或说话。

entries.definition: heavy like lead and dull in spirit or movement; its root is the metal lead, so it only shares meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，意为「如铅般沉重、无生气」；其词根是金属铅，与 ponderous 只是意义相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: swollen and pompous in language, dull by being overblown.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指文辞浮夸臃肿而显得沉闷。

normalIntro.en: Ponderous sits on the Latin scale of pondus, a weight: whatever it describes has to be lifted.
normalIntro.cn: ponderous 扎根在拉丁语表示「重量」的 pondus 上：它形容的一切都得费力气才抬得动。

normal.en: The same root gives ponder, to weigh a thought in the mind before acting.
normal.cn: 同根词 ponder 意为「沉思」，就是在动手前把想法掂量一番。

normal.en: Ponderous usually goes before a noun and has no -er form, so say more ponderous instead.
normal.cn: ponderous 常放在名词前，且不用 -er 比较级，比较时用 more ponderous。

normal.en: The adverb ponderously takes -ly, as in a lorry moving ponderously uphill.
normal.cn: 副词 ponderously 加 -ly 构成，如卡车「缓慢吃力地」爬坡。

normal.en: Ponderous pairs with heavy objects and slow machines, as in ponderous machinery.
normal.cn: ponderous 常与沉重物体、迟缓机械搭配，如 ponderous machinery（笨重的机械）。

normal.en: Compare weighty, which praises ideas, while ponderous criticises heaviness in style.
normal.cn: 对比 weighty：weighty 多赞美观点有分量，ponderous 则批评文风沉重乏味。

abstract.en: Picture a stone statue being shifted one centimetre at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一尊石像被一厘米一厘米地挪动。

abstract.en: Imagine a tortoise carrying its house up a gravel path.
abstract.cn: 想象一只乌龟背着壳，在碎石小路上缓慢爬行。

abstract.en: Picture a grey ledger so thick that reading one page feels like lifting it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚得发灰的账簿，读一页都像在举起它。

examples.en: The museum staff hate moving the ponderous marble sarcophagus.
examples.cn: 博物馆的员工很怕搬动那具沉重的大理石石棺。

examples.en: She avoided the ponderous vocabulary that makes academic papers unreadable.
examples.cn: 她避免使用那种让学术论文难以读完的冗长词汇。

examples.en: The old water wheel turned ponderously in the mill stream.
examples.cn: 旧水车在磨坊的溪流里沉重而迟缓地转着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「庞得若死」——庞然大物，重得人要累死：沉重的、笨重的。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pondus（重量）→ ponderare（称重、掂量）→ ponderosus（沉重的）→ 中古英语 ponderous，核心义「有分量、压得人吃力」。

sensesIntro.en: Ponderous grows out of one scale: first an object too heavy to move, then motion that is slow, then clumsiness, then dull prose, then weight felt in institutions and the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: ponderous 从一个秤盘般的画面展开：先是重得搬不动的物体，再是缓慢的动作、笨拙的举止、沉闷的文笔，最后是机构与心事所感到的重量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone figure being pushed across a floor while everyone strains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一尊石像被推着在地面上挪动，人人都在使劲。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: weight on the scale gives a heavy thing and, at its largest, a massive shape without grace.
branches.cn: 物体线：秤上沉下去的重量给出沉重之物，放大到极致就是臃肿而无美感的形体。

branches.en: THE MOTION: a weight that moves travels slowly and heavily.
branches.cn: 动作线：会移动的重量走起来慢而沉。

branches.en: THE BODY: a body weighed down cannot turn neatly, so heaviness becomes clumsiness in manner.
branches.cn: 身体线：被压住的身体转不灵便，重量于是成了举止上的笨拙。

branches.en: THE WORD AND THE OFFICE: heavy prose and heavy procedure both make readers wait.
branches.cn: 文字与机构线：沉重的文笔与沉重的程序，都让人不得不等待。

branches.en: THE MOOD: great weight reads as solemnity in a hall and as gloom on a quiet room.
branches.cn: 氛围线：巨大的重量在大厅里读作庄重，在安静的房间里则读作压抑。

intro.en: Ponderous is Latin pondus plus the suffix -ous, and English builds ponder, preponderance, pound and the -poise of equipoise around the same root.
intro.cn: ponderous 是拉丁语 pondus 加后缀 -ous 构成，英语围绕同一词根还构成 ponder、preponderance、pound，以及 equipoise 中的 -poise。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere means to hang, pondus means a weight, and ponderare means to weigh.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂，pondus 意为重量，ponderare 意为称重。

items.example: Pondus is the noun behind English pound.
items.exampleCN: pondus 是英语 pound 背后的名词。

items.example: Ponderare means to put a question on the scale.
items.exampleCN: ponderare 意为把一个问题放上秤去称。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix turns pondus into ponderosus.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把 pondus 变成 ponderosus。

items.example: Ponderous keeps the sense of weight.
items.exampleCN: ponderous 保留了「重」的含义。

items.example: To ponder is to weigh a thought slowly.
items.exampleCN: ponder 就是把一个想法慢慢称一称。

items.example: Pre- plus weight gives preponderance.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 加上重量，构成 preponderance。

items.example: What outweighs the rest is preponderant.
items.exampleCN: 分量压过其余者，就是 preponderant。

items.example: Pound comes from Latin pondus by way of Old English.
items.exampleCN: pound 经由古英语，源自拉丁语 pondus。

items.example: Equi- with weight gives equilibrio in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 equi- 与「重量」结合，构成拉丁语 equilibrio。

items.example: Equipoise means the two halves weigh the same.
items.exampleCN: equipoise 意为两边分量相等。

latinEntries.example: Pondus gives the English noun pound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pondus 派生出英语名词 pound。

latinEntries.example: Pendere hangs a thing on the scale.

latinEntries.exampleCN: ponderare 派生出英语动词 ponder。

latinEntries.example: Ponderosus is the direct source of ponderous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ponderosus 是 ponderous 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 矮种马；小马；赛马用语中的「马」；小杯（酒）；一小束香蕉；马尾辫
definition_en: a small horse, or one of several small things named after it, such as a pony glass of drink
core_image: 围场里一匹矮小的马驮着孩子，四蹄短而结实地跑过草地
scene: 乡间集市上，牧场主让孩子骑上一匹短腿小马绕圈，马鬃被风吹得乱抖。For two pounds the farmer let each child ride the sturdy little pony twice around the ring, and the queue did not seem to shrink all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 pony 是「矮种马、小马」（第 1 个义项：体型矮小的马）；句意：农夫收两英镑就让每个孩子在围栏里骑两圈那匹结实的小马，整下午队伍好像都没变短。

pos.zh: 矮种马；小马；（赛马）马；小众杯（酒）；（香蕉的）一小串；马尾辫

collocations.zh: 驿马快信（十九世纪美国西部邮驿）

derivatives.zh: 由 pony + tail 构成，义为「马尾辫」
由 ponytail 加 -ed 构成，义为「扎着马尾辫的」
由 pony 加 -ish 构成，义为「像小马的」
由 pony 加 -ism 构成，义为「（赛马中）下暗注的做法」

senses.title: A small breed of horse
senses.definition: a small horse, especially one below about fourteen hands high
senses.definitionCN: 体型矮小的马，尤指身高不足约十四掌的马
senses.example: The children fed the ponies in the field beyond the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在围栏外的地里喂那些小马。
senses.why: The word first named this sturdy little horse, and every other sense of pony is a small thing seen through that image.
senses.whyCN: pony 最初指的就是这种结实的小马，其余义项都是借着这个画面来看「小东西」。

senses.title: A mount in horse racing talk
senses.definition: a horse being ridden or bet on, used especially by racing people
senses.definitionCN: 被骑乘或被下注的马，赛马圈里的行话
senses.example: The trainer will not say which pony she expects to win.
senses.exampleCN: 那位驯马师不会说哪匹马是她看好的。
senses.why: Racing culture talks of every mount as a horse, and the small nickname became a neutral word for a racehorse.
senses.whyCN: 赛马圈把任何一匹坐骑都说成「马」，小马这个昵称就成了赛马的普通称谓。

senses.title: A very small glass of drink
senses.definition: a small measure of alcoholic drink, served in a small glass
senses.definitionCN: 份量很小的酒，用小杯盛着喝
senses.example: He ordered a pony of brandy and drank it standing up.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一小杯白兰地，站着就喝掉了。
senses.why: A bar measure is small beside the full glass, and the little horse gave the name for the little serving.
senses.whyCN: 酒吧里的份量比起满杯要小，小马的形象就转给了小的份量。

senses.title: A small group of bananas
senses.definition: a small cluster of bananas, larger than a single finger and often left unsold at the bottom of the bunch
senses.definitionCN: 一小串香蕉，比单个香蕉多，常是整串卖剩落在底下的小串
senses.example: The market trader threw in a pony of bananas with the shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 摊主顺手搭了一小串香蕉给顾客。
senses.why: Produce trade called anything smaller than a full bunch a pony, following the same small-thing pattern.
senses.whyCN: 果蔬行业把不足整串的东西都叫作 pony，沿用同一套「小」的构词思路。

senses.title: A short curtain or a small object
senses.definition: a short piece of cloth or a small extra object, such as a short theatre curtain or a small added engine unit on a tram
senses.definitionCN: 一小段布或额外的小物件，如戏台的短幕、有轨电车后挂的小发动机
senses.example: The stage was fitted with a pair of ponies to drop before the act.
senses.exampleCN: 戏台装了一对短幕，在那一幕开场前放下。
senses.why: Theatre and railway workshops used pony for any small piece set beside a larger one, as a pony stands beside full horses.
senses.whyCN: 戏台与铁路工场用 pony 称大件旁边的小件，正如小马站在高头大马旁边。

senses.title: A small part of a task
senses.definition: a small task or a minor part of a larger piece of work, as in pony and trap meaning a small job added to a big one
senses.definitionCN: 大任务中的小活儿，习语 pony and trap 借押韵表示添加的小件工作
senses.example: Building the bridge was one thing, but paving the last footpath was a right pony.
senses.exampleCN: 建桥是一回事，可最后那段人行道也是件不省心的小活儿。
senses.why: Cockney rhyming slang matched pony and trap with its partner sense, so pony came to mean a small attached task.
senses.whyCN: 伦敦押韵俚语把 pony and trap 与其押韵对象配对，于是 pony 指附带的琐碎差事。

senses.title: A horse tail of hair
senses.definition: hair tied and gathered at the back of the head so that it hangs like a horse tail
senses.definitionCN: 把头发束在脑后下垂，形如马尾
senses.example: She tied her hair into a tight ponytail before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前她把头发扎成紧马尾。
senses.why: The ponytail is named for the shape it copies, and the small horse shows up in the hair itself.
senses.whyCN: 马尾辫是照着小马的尾巴取名的，小马的形象就落在头发上。

senses.title: A relay rider in old postal service
senses.definition: a rider who carried mail by relays of horses, as in the pony express
senses.definitionCN: 靠着换马接力递送邮件的骑手，如美国驿马快信
senses.example: The last pony reached the relay station at nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一名驿马骑手在黄昏时分到达接力站。
senses.why: The mail riders rode light horses in relay, and the smallness of the mount gave the service its name.
senses.whyCN: 邮差骑轻便的马一站接一站，坐骑之小给了这项服务以名称。

intro.en: Pony is a Scottish and northern English word of uncertain origin, first written down in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: pony 是苏格兰与英格兰北部的词，词源不确定，首次见于十七世纪的文字记录。

items.en: Powny is recorded in Scottish and northern English texts for a small horse.
items.cn: 苏格兰与英格兰北部文献记下 powny 一词，指小马。

items.en: Its earlier source is uncertain; one guess is an old French word for a foal.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；一种猜测是古法语中表示小马驹的词。

items.en: The spelling pony settles, and the word names the small horse in general use.
items.cn: 拼写定为 pony，这个词在通用语中指小马。

items.en: Pony spreads to small measures: a small glass of drink and small lots of fruit.
items.cn: pony 扩展到「小份量」：小杯酒、小串水果。

items.en: Pony grows into names for the pony express, ponytail and racing slang.
items.cn: pony 进一步构成驿马快信、马尾辫与赛马行话等说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the horse and the whole family of small things.
items.cn: 现代英语既保留「小马」，也保留了一整族「小东西」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives of pony; the near-meaning group gathers other small horses and small measures.
note.cn: 形近组收 pony 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收其他小型马匹与小型份量的说法。

entries.definition: hair gathered and tied at the back of the head.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「马尾辫」。

entries.definition: the plural of pony.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，义为「多匹小马」。

entries.definition: a small horse and cart; in rhyming slang it names a small attached task.
entries.definitionCN: 词组，义为「小马拉双轮车」，押韵俚语中借指附带的小活儿。

entries.definition: a member of the police; the ending -man only looks similar and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「警察」；词尾与 pony 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a very young horse, of any breed.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，指幼马、马驹，不限马种，强调年龄而非体型。

entries.definition: an old or worn-out horse.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，口语中指老马、劣马，带贬义。

entries.definition: a horse used for carrying loads.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指驮运货物的马。

entries.definition: a very small measure of a strong drink.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指极小杯的烈酒，与 pony 的小杯义相近。

entries.definition: a group of bananas growing together.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指一整串香蕉，与小串的 pony 相对。

normalIntro.en: Pony is heard first as a small horse, and the whole family of small things follows from that picture.
normalIntro.cn: pony 首先让人想到一匹小马，随后一整套「小东西」的说法都从这个画面延伸出来。

normal.en: The plural of pony is ponies, so the -y becomes -ies after a consonant.
normal.cn: pony 的复数是 ponies，辅音后的 -y 要变成 -ies。

normal.en: Pony express names the fast mail relays of the American West.
normal.cn: pony express 指美国西部的驿马快信。

normal.en: A Shetland pony is one of the smallest breeds, used for children.
normal.cn: Shetland pony 是最小的马种之一，常给孩子骑。

normal.en: Ponytail is pony plus tail, since the hair hangs like a horse tail.
normal.cn: ponytail 由 pony 加 tail 组成，因为头发垂得像马尾巴。

normal.en: Compare horse, which is larger and more neutral, while pony is small and friendly.
normal.cn: 对比 horse：horse 更大、更中性，pony 则小而亲切。

abstract.en: Picture a short-legged horse trotting around a ring with a child on its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一匹短腿的马驮着孩子围着围栏小跑。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny glass of amber drink set beside a full mug.
abstract.cn: 想象一小杯琥珀色的酒放在满满的酒杯旁。

abstract.en: Picture a ponytail swinging as the rider crosses the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象骑手冲过终点时马尾辫随之一甩。

examples.en: A pony can carry an adult, but it is bred mainly for children.
examples.cn: 小马也能驮成年人，但主要培育给孩子骑。

examples.en: The pub serves a pony of whisky to those who must drive home.
examples.cn: 那家酒馆会给要开车回家的人上一小杯威士忌。

examples.en: She pinned her ponies back before putting on the helmet.
examples.cn: 她戴上头盔前把马尾辫别到了脑后。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡尼」——一匹小马爬长长的坡也不累，稳稳驮着孩子：矮种马、小马。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 苏格兰与英格兰北部词 powny（小马，词源不确定）→ 英语 pony，核心义「小而结实的马」，再泛化为「小的东西、小的份量」。

sensesIntro.en: Pony starts as the small sturdy horse, then lends its small size to a racing mount, a small glass, a small bunch of bananas, a short curtain, a small task, a horse tail of hair and a mail rider.
sensesIntro.cn: pony 本指小而结实的马，再把这份「小」借给赛马坐骑、小杯酒、小串香蕉、短幕、小任务、马尾辫与驿马骑手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short-legged horse trotting with a child in the saddle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一匹短腿的小马驮着孩子在草地上跑。

branches.en: THE HORSE: a small breed, and by extension the light relay mount of the mail riders.
branches.cn: 马匹线：矮小的马种，延伸到驿马骑手所骑的轻便坐骑。

branches.en: THE TRACK: racing people call every runner a pony, whatever its size.
branches.cn: 赛道线：赛马圈不论马的大小，都叫它 pony。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a small glass of drink and a small bunch of bananas both borrow the small horse.
branches.cn: 份量线：小杯酒与小串香蕉都借用了小马之小。

branches.en: THE SMALL PART: a short curtain or a small added job is the pony beside the full horse.
branches.cn: 小件线：短幕或另外加的小活儿，都是高头大马旁边的那匹小马。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: hair tied to hang like a tail keeps the horse image in plain view.
branches.cn: 形状线：束在脑后下垂的头发，把马的意象直接摆在眼前。

intro.en: Pony is a Germanic-Scottish word of uncertain root, and English builds ponytail, ponytailed, pony express and pony and trap on it.
intro.cn: pony 是出自苏格兰的日耳曼系词，词根不确定，英语在其上构成 ponytail、ponytailed、pony express 与 pony and trap。

latinIntro.en: Pony has no trustworthy Latin origin, so this list notes the two Latin words sometimes guessed as its source rather than claiming them as ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: pony 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，这里只列出偶尔被猜测为源头的两个拉丁词，而不主张它们就是祖先。

items.example: Pony is the base for the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pony 是整个词族的基础。

items.meaning: plural of words ending in consonant plus y
items.meaningCN: 辅音加 y 结尾名词的复数词尾
items.example: The suffix turns pony into ponies.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ies 把 pony 变成 ponies。

items.example: Pony plus tail gives ponytail.
items.exampleCN: pony 加 tail 构成 ponytail。

items.example: The ponytail copies the shape of a horse tail.
items.exampleCN: 马尾辫照着马尾巴的形状。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms ponytailed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 ponytailed。

items.example: Ponytailed describes a person with tied hair.
items.exampleCN: ponytailed 形容扎着马尾辫的人。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms ponyish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 构成 ponyish。

items.example: Pony plus express gives pony express.
items.exampleCN: pony 加 express 构成 pony express。

items.example: Pony and trap is a small carriage and its horse.
items.exampleCN: pony and trap 指小马与轻便双轮马车。

latinEntries.example: Pullus is sometimes guessed behind pony, but the link is not proved.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 偶尔有人猜测 pullus 是 pony 的源头，但这一联系并未被证实。

latinEntries.example: Equus names the horse in Latin but gives English equestrian, not pony.
latinEntries.exampleCN: equus 在拉丁语中指马，但派生的是英语 equestrian，而不是 pony。

definition_zh: 爆米花；爆裂玉米（粒）；卖爆米花的场所
definition_en: corn grains heated until they burst into light white puffs, eaten as a snack
core_image: 锅盖被玉米粒顶得直跳，一粒粒黄玉米炸开成白色的花
scene: 电影开场前，大厅里飘着黄油香，有人抱着一大桶玉米花边笑边往嘴里塞。We shared a huge tub of popcorn in the dark, and the smell of butter seemed to hang over half the row.
sceneCN: 这里 popcorn 是「爆米花」（第 1 个义项：加热后炸开、当零食吃的玉米花）；句意：我们在黑暗里合吃一大桶爆米花，黄油味几乎飘满了半排座位。

pos.zh: 爆米花；爆裂玉米（粒）；（影院）卖爆米花的柜台

collocations.zh: 爆米花天花板（喷射状颗粒饰面）
爆米花虾（一口大小的炸虾）

derivatives.zh: popcorn 的第一部分，义为「砰然爆开」，取爆破声
由 pop 加 -er 构成，义为「爆米花机」，如 popcorn popper
由 popping（爆开的）加 corn 构成，义为「爆裂玉米」
popcorn 的第二部分，英式英语中指谷粒、小麦，美式英语中指玉米

senses.title: Puffed corn as a snack
senses.definition: corn grains heated until they burst into white puffs, eaten by the handful as a snack
senses.definitionCN: 玉米粒加热后炸成白色蓬松小球，抓着当零食吃
senses.example: Children threw popcorn at each other until the film started.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开场前，孩子们互相扔爆米花。
senses.why: The word is a sound joined to a grain: pop names the burst, corn the seed, so the snack is the grain made to pop.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「声音」加「谷粒」：pop 表示爆裂的声响，corn 表示谷粒，零食就是被炸开的谷粒。

senses.title: The grain used for popping
senses.definition: a variety of maize with hard, small kernels that burst well when heated
senses.definitionCN: 一种玉米品种，籽粒小而硬，加热时容易爆开
senses.example: You need proper popcorn, not sweetcorn, for the pan to crackle.
senses.exampleCN: 要用专门的爆裂玉米，而不是甜玉米，锅才会噼啪作响。
senses.why: Since the burst depends on the grain, the same word names the raw material that is bought by the bag.
senses.whyCN: 能不能炸开取决于谷粒本身，于是同一个词也指成袋买来的那种专用玉米。

senses.title: A place selling it
senses.definition: a stall or counter in a cinema that sells popped corn
senses.definitionCN: 影院里售卖爆米花的摊位或柜台
senses.example: The popcorn is next to the ticket desk, so nobody can walk past it.
senses.exampleCN: 爆米花柜台就在售票台旁边，谁都绕不过去。
senses.why: English often names a counter by what it sells, so the snack becomes the shop that sells it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用卖的东西来称呼柜台，于是零食的名称变成了售卖它的场所。

senses.title: Light entertainment for a crowd
senses.definition: inexpensive popular entertainment that is enjoyed quickly and forgotten, like cinema during the popcorn boom
senses.definitionCN: 廉价快速的大众娱乐，像爆米花兴盛时期的电影那样看完就忘
senses.example: Critics complained that the festival was turning into popcorn for tourists.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家抱怨说，这个艺术节正变成专供游客消遣的玩意儿。
senses.why: As cinema boomed, popcorn came to stand for the whole easy pleasure of a night at the pictures.
senses.whyCN: 随着电影繁荣，popcorn 也成了「在影院轻松消遣一晚」的整体象征。

senses.title: A spreading pattern of flecks
senses.titleCN: 爆米花纹理（喷射状颗粒饰面）
senses.definition: a decorative surface sprayed with small lumps, such as a popcorn ceiling or a popcorn paint finish
senses.definitionCN: 喷涂出许多小颗粒的装饰表面，如爆米花天花板或爆米花涂料
senses.example: The flat was priced low because of the popcorn ceilings.
senses.exampleCN: 那套公寓因为天花板是爆米花纹理，所以标价偏低。
senses.why: The scattered white puffs look like the lumps on a sprayed ceiling, so the pattern borrows the snack name.
senses.whyCN: 散落的白色蓬松小球像喷射天花板上的颗粒，于是这种纹理借用了零食的名字。

senses.title: Bite-sized pieces of food
senses.definition: small pieces of food that puff and crunch, as in popcorn shrimp or popcorn chicken
senses.definitionCN: 小而蓬松脆口的一块块食物，如爆米花虾、爆米花鸡
senses.example: The bar snack menu is mostly popcorn shrimp and popcorn chicken.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒吧的小食单上主要是爆米花虾和爆米花鸡。
senses.why: Anything puffed, clustered and bite-sized repeats the shape of popped corn, so its name is taken over.
senses.whyCN: 凡是蓬松成簇、一口大小、外脆内嫩的食物，都在重复玉米花的形状，于是名字被借用过去。

senses.title: A corn snack made in a pot
senses.definition: the same snack popped at home in a pan or popper with a lid, a family ritual rather than shop food
senses.definitionCN: 在家里用带盖的锅或爆米花机爆出的同类零食，是一种家庭仪式而非商店食品
senses.example: On rainy Sundays we made popcorn on the stove with a lid that rattled.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨的星期天，我们会用盖子噼啪乱响的锅在炉子上爆玉米花。
senses.why: The kitchen version keeps the original sound image: the lid rattles as the grain pops, which is the whole word in a pan.
senses.whyCN: 家庭做法保留了最初的听觉画面：盖子被粒粒爆声震得直响，一个词都在锅里了。

senses.title: A sign that houses are popping up
senses.titleCN: 忽如雨后春笋般出现的事物
senses.definition: a thing that appears suddenly in many places, as cheap cinema houses did across towns
senses.definitionCN: 突然在许多地方出现的事物，正如当年城镇里一夜间冒出的廉价影院
senses.example: Small coffee chains are popping up like popcorn on every corner.
senses.exampleCN: 小型咖啡连锁店像爆米花一样在街头巷角冒出来。
senses.why: One popped kernel sets several others cracking in the same pan, which is exactly how sudden growth is pictured.
senses.whyCN: 锅里一粒爆开就会引来旁边好几粒跟着噼啪爆裂，这正是一夜之间四处冒出的样子。

intro.en: Popcorn joins pop, the sound of a burst, to corn, an old word for a grain; it is usually dated to the early nineteenth century.
intro.cn: popcorn 由 pop（爆裂声）与 corn（古英语中的「谷粒」）合成，一般认为出现在十九世纪初。

items.en: Corn means a grain or a seed, not only maize, and names wheat or oats in England.
items.cn: 古英语 corn 泛指谷粒、种子，不只指玉米，在英格兰指小麦或燕麦。

items.en: Pop grows up as a word for a sudden burst and the sound it makes.
items.cn: pop 在十六世纪发展出「突然爆裂」及其声响的含义。

items.en: In America corn comes to mean maize, and heated maize becomes a popular snack.
items.cn: 在美洲，corn 渐渐指玉米，加热爆开的玉米成了流行零食。

items.en: The compound popcorn is usually first recorded in a dictionary around the eighteen twenties.
items.cn: 复合词 popcorn 通常被认为在十九世纪二十年代前后的词典里首次收录。

items.en: Popping corn becomes a household and street trade as cheap pans reach ordinary homes.
items.cn: 随着便宜的爆锅进入普通人家，爆玉米成了家庭与街头小生意。

items.en: Cinemas made popcorn the standard snack and gave the word its wider popular senses.
items.cn: 影院让爆米花成为标准零食，也把这个词推向了更广泛的大众含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives built on pop and corn; the near-meaning group gathers neighbouring snack and grain words.
note.cn: 形近组收由 pop 与 corn 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收周边的零食与谷物词。

entries.definition: a pan or machine for popping corn.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「爆米花锅、爆米花机」。

entries.definition: maize of a kind that puffs well when heated.
entries.definitionCN: 同源短语，义为「爆裂玉米」。

entries.definition: a grain in British English, maize in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，英式英语指谷粒，美式英语指玉米。

entries.definition: appealing to ordinary people; it begins with pop- but comes from Latin populus, people.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「民粹的、迎合大众的」；虽然以 pop- 开头，却出自拉丁语 populus（人民），只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: rice grains heated until they swell into light grains.
entries.definitionCN: 同类食品，指加热膨胀的米粒。

entries.definition: a thin dry biscuit eaten as a snack.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指薄脆饼干，与爆米花同属脆口零食。

entries.definition: flakes made of maize and eaten at breakfast.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指玉米片，与爆米花共用 corn 表示玉米。

entries.definition: the plant and grain that popcorn is made from, in British use.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，英式英语中指玉米这种作物，是爆米花的原料。

entries.definition: a small sugar sweet; it only parodies the popcorn pastime joke, without sharing the root.
entries.definitionCN: 同类词，指小颗软糖；这里只是模仿爆米花的谐趣说法，词源无关。

normalIntro.en: Popcorn is a sound word plus a grain word, so the popping itself is the best way to remember it.
normalIntro.cn: popcorn 是一个「声音词」加一个「谷物词」，所以爆开的那阵响声就是最好的记忆线索。

normal.en: Pop imitates the crack of a kernel, so popcorn is literally corn that pops.
normal.cn: pop 模仿玉米粒爆裂的响声，popcorn 字面就是「会爆的玉米」。

normal.en: In British English corn means any grain, while in American English it means maize.
normal.cn: corn 在英式英语里泛指谷物，在美式英语里专指玉米。

normal.en: The snack is uncountable, so we say a tub of popcorn, not a popcorn.
normal.cn: 作为零食时 popcorn 不可数，要说 a tub of popcorn，而不说 a popcorn。

normal.en: A popcorn movie is loud, easy fun for a cinema crowd.
normal.cn: popcorn movie 指热闹、轻松、适合影院取乐的片子。

normal.en: A popcorn ceiling is sprayed with small lumps that look like popped corn.
normal.cn: popcorn ceiling 是喷满小颗粒、形似爆米花的天花板。

abstract.en: Picture a lid hopping as the first kernel cracks in the pan.
abstract.cn: 想象锅里第一粒玉米裂开，盖子被顶得直跳。

abstract.en: Imagine a bucket seen from above, white puffs packed to the brim.
abstract.cn: 想象从上方看一大桶爆米花，白色小球堆到桶沿。

abstract.en: Picture a red and white striped cart sending out a smell of butter.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆红白条纹的推车，飘出浓浓黄油味。

examples.en: The theatre sells sweet and salty popcorn in the same size of bucket.
examples.cn: 那家影院把甜味和咸味爆米花装在同样大小的桶里出售。

examples.en: Keep the lid on while you heat the popcorn, or the kernels will fly out.
examples.cn: 加热爆米花时要盖好锅盖，不然玉米粒会蹦出来。

examples.en: Reviewers dismissed the new series as popcorn, all noise and no plot.
examples.cn: 评论者把这部新剧斥为纯粹消遣，只有热闹没有情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啪扑空」——玉米粒啪一声爆开，壳就扑空了：爆米花。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: pop（爆裂声）+ corn（古英语「谷粒」）→ 美洲英语 popcorn（爆开的玉米），核心义「一声爆响，谷粒开花」。

sensesIntro.en: Popcorn begins with a grain that bursts at a sound, then names the snack, the grain, the shop, the night out, the speckled pattern, bite-sized food, home popping and any sudden spread.
sensesIntro.cn: popcorn 起于「一声爆响、谷粒开花」，随后指零食、原料、售卖柜台、消遣之夜的象征、颗粒纹理、一口大小的食物、家常爆制，以及任何突然蔓延的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lid jumping on a pan as yellow corn splits into white puffs.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅盖被顶得直跳，黄玉米炸成一朵朵白花。

branches.en: THE SNACK: the puffed corn eaten by the handful, whether bought or made at home in a lid-shaking pan.
branches.cn: 零食线：一把把抓着吃的玉米花，不论是买来的还是家里盖着锅爆出来的。

branches.en: THE GRAIN: only the hard, small kernels burst, so the recipe names the raw material too.
branches.cn: 原料线：只有小而硬的籽粒才爆得开，所以这个词也指原料本身。

branches.en: THE EVENING OUT: the counter that sells popcorn and the easy pleasure of the whole trip stand for cinema culture.
branches.cn: 消遣之夜：卖爆米花的柜台与整个轻松取乐的过程，都成了影院文化的象征。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: white scattered lumps and bite-sized crunchy pieces both copy the look of popped corn.
branches.cn: 形状线：散落的白色颗粒与一口大小的脆块，都在模仿爆米花的模样。

branches.en: THE PACE: one kernel sets off the next, which pictures things popping up all at once.
branches.cn: 节奏线：一粒爆开引来下一粒，这正描绘了事物一下子纷纷冒出的图景。

intro.en: Popcorn is a native compound of pop and corn, and English extends it through popper, popping corn and popcorn movie.
intro.cn: popcorn 是 pop 与 corn 组成的本族复合词，英语再通过 popper、popping corn、popcorn movie 等延伸出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Neither half of popcorn is Latin, so this list records the Latin and Greek sources of the nearest grain words rather than ancestors of popcorn.
latinIntro.cn: popcorn 的两半都不是拉丁语，这里记录的是最接近的谷物词的拉丁语与希腊语来源，而不是 popcorn 的祖先。

items.meaning: to burst with a small sharp sound
items.example: Pop imitates the sound of the kernel splitting.
items.exampleCN: pop 模仿玉米粒裂开的声响。

items.example: Corn is an old West Germanic grain word.
items.exampleCN: corn 是一个古老的西日耳曼语谷物词。

items.example: Popcorn joins the sound to the grain.
items.exampleCN: popcorn 把声音与谷粒合在一起。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms popper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 popper。

items.example: A popper does the popping for you.
items.exampleCN: 爆米花机替你把玉米爆开。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms popping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 popping。

items.example: Cornflakes shares corn in the American sense.
items.exampleCN: cornflakes 共用 corn 的「玉米」义。

items.example: Popcorn plus movie gives popcorn movie.
items.exampleCN: popcorn 加 movie 构成 popcorn movie。

items.meaning: the top surface of a room
items.example: Popcorn plus ceiling names a textured ceiling.
items.exampleCN: popcorn 加 ceiling 指颗粒饰面天花板。

latinEntries.example: Granum is Latin for grain, a cousin of corn rather than its parent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: granum 是拉丁语「谷粒」，与 corn 是同源远亲，而非其来源。

latinEntries.meaning: a kind of grain, possibly spelt
latinEntries.meaningCN: 某种谷物，可能指斯佩耳特小麦
latinEntries.example: Greek zeia is the source of Latin zea, a grain word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 zeia 是拉丁语 zea（谷物）的来源。

definition_zh: 杨树；白杨木
definition_en: a tall tree with a rising trunk and soft leaves that flutter in the wind, or the light wood of this tree
core_image: 一排笔直高瘦的杨树站在河岸上，叶子在风里不停地抖
scene: 夏天，河边的小路两旁种满了高高的杨树，风一吹，叶子就沙沙作响。Tall poplars line the riverside path, and their leaves rustle whenever the wind blows.
sceneCN: 这里 poplar 是「杨树」（第 1 个义项：一种高瘦、叶子会随风抖动的树）；句意：河边小路两旁长着高高的杨树，风一吹叶子就沙沙响。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，指多棵杨树或成片杨林
黑杨：由颜色词与 poplar 构成的复合名词
北美鹅掌楸：并非派生词，只是常被与杨树放在一起比较的树名

senses.title: The tree with fluttering leaves
senses.definition: a tall column shaped tree whose broad soft leaves tremble in the slightest breeze
senses.definitionCN: 一种树身高瘦、叶片宽而柔软、微风一吹就抖动的树木
senses.example: A line of poplars shields the village from the strong north wind.
senses.exampleCN: 一排杨树把村子挡住了强劲的北风。
senses.why: The word names the tree by the shaking of its leaves, and the trembling leaves are the picture that ties the plant to the adjective for shaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用叶子不停抖动的特点来命名这种树，而「抖动」正是它与表示摇晃的形容词共享的意象。

senses.title: The timber of the tree
senses.definition: the pale light wood of a poplar, used for boxes, crates and paper pulp
senses.definitionCN: 杨树砍下后得到的浅色轻软木材，可做箱子、板条箱和纸浆
senses.example: The factory packs fruit in lightweight poplar crates.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用轻便的杨木箱装水果。
senses.why: Once a tree is named, its material takes the same name, so the tall living tree becomes a stack of pale boards.
senses.whyCN: 一种树有了名字，它的木材也沿用这个名字，于是一棵活的高树就变成了成堆的浅色木板。

senses.title: The poplars of a riverside road
senses.definition: a row of poplars planted along a road, canal or riverside as a windbreak or landmark
senses.definitionCN: 沿大路、运河或河岸成排栽种的杨树，用来挡风或充当地标
senses.example: The poplars along the canal mark the old county border.
senses.exampleCN: 运河边的那排杨树标出了旧的县界。
senses.why: Because poplars grow fast and stand straight, people plant them in lines, and the line of trees itself becomes a familiar landmark in many landscapes.
senses.whyCN: 杨树长得快又笔直，人们习惯成排种植，这一排树在许多地方风景里就成了一眼能认出的地标。

intro.en: Poplar comes from Latin populus, the name of this tree, and it is the same Latin word that sits inside populate and population.
intro.cn: poplar 来自拉丁语 populus（杨树），而这个拉丁词也正是 populate 与 population 所包含的词根。

items.en: Populus is the classical Latin name for the poplar tree.
items.cn: populus 是古典拉丁语对杨树的称呼。

items.en: Old French keeps the word as poplier, naming the tree.
items.cn: 古法语把该词保留为 poplier，仍是树名。

items.en: Middle English records popler as a common tree name.
items.cn: 中古英语以 popler 记录这种常见的树。

items.en: The spelling settles into poplar, close to the Latin source.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 poplar，与拉丁语原形更接近。

items.en: Latin populus for the tree and populus for the people are separate words of the same spelling, so poplar is not related to the voters and inhabitants inside populate.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表示树木的 populus 与表示人民的 populus 只是同形异义的两种词，所以 poplar 与 populate 里的人民、居民并不相关。

note.en: Poplar looks like populate and population but comes from the tree word, while its neighbours are other tall roadside trees and the family of trembling leaf words.
note.cn: poplar 看上去与 populate、population 相似，却来自树名；它的近邻是别的路旁高树，以及表示「叶子抖动」的一组词。

entries.definition: a smooth light cotton or silk fabric
entries.definitionCN: 平纹细布；府绸（只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自法语 nome de papeline）

entries.definition: not a real English word, listed only to warn against a common misspelling of popular
entries.definitionCN: 并非真实英语词，列出只为提醒它常被误写成 popular 的拼写（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: splendid ceremonial display
entries.definitionCN: 排场；炫耀（只是发音相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语 pompa）

entries.definition: a related tall tree whose leaves quiver almost without a breeze
entries.definitionCN: 白杨；山杨：与杨树同类，叶子几乎无风也会颤动

entries.definition: a riverside tree with long slender branches
entries.definitionCN: 柳树：常种在河边的另一种树

entries.definition: a slender tree with pale peeling bark
entries.definitionCN: 桦树：树身细、树皮发白易剥

normalIntro.en: Poplar is first of all a tree name, and the leaf that shakes in the wind is the memory hook that also explains the related adjective.
normalIntro.cn: poplar 首先是一个树名，风里不停抖动的叶子既是最好的记忆钩子，也解释了同源的形容词。

normal.en: A poplar is a tall tree with soft leaves that tremble in any breeze.
normal.cn: poplar 是一种高大、叶子柔软、稍有风就抖动的树。

normal.en: Latin populus named the tree, so poplar has nothing to do with voters.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 populus 指的是这种树，所以 poplar 与「选民」无关。

normal.en: A row of poplars along a road works as a natural windbreak.
normal.cn: 路边成排的杨树就是天然的挡风墙。

normal.en: Poplar wood is pale and light, so it is used for crates and paper pulp.
normal.cn: 杨木色浅质轻，常用来做木箱和纸浆。

normal.en: Compare aspen and willow: all three are tall riverside trees, but only the poplar carries the tree name in its Latin root.
normal.cn: 对比 aspen 与 willow：三者都常长在水边，但只有 poplar 的拉丁词根本身就是树名。

abstract.en: Picture one silver leaf flipping over and over on a bare branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一片银色的叶子在光秃的枝条上不停地翻动。

abstract.en: Think of a sawmill turning pale boards into fruit boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象锯木厂把浅色的木板做成水果箱。

abstract.en: See an avenue of upright green towers guiding you along a canal.
abstract.cn: 想象运河旁一列笔直的绿色高塔为你指路。

examples.en: Tall poplars line both sides of the country road.
examples.cn: 乡村公路两旁种着高大的杨树。

examples.en: The carpenter chose poplar because it is light and easy to cut.
examples.cn: 木匠选了杨木，因为它又轻又容易加工。

examples.en: White poplar leaves show a silvery underside when the wind turns them.
examples.cn: 银白杨的叶子被风吹翻时露出银白色的背面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡普拉」——杨树长在河坡上，风吹就「扑啦」作响；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 populus（杨树）→ 古法语 poplier → 中古英语 popler → 现代英语 poplar；与表示「人民」的拉丁语 populus 同形但不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Poplar first names the living tree, then its pale timber, and finally the rows of trees people plant as windbreaks.
sensesIntro.cn: poplar 先指活着的杨树，再指它浅色的木材，最后指人们成排栽种用来挡风的那一列杨树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall slim tree whose soft leaves flip in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵高瘦的树，柔软的叶子在风中不停翻动。

branches.en: The tree itself is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 杨树本身是日常义项。

branches.en: The timber sense moves from plant to material.
branches.cn: 杨木义项从植物转向材料。

branches.en: The planted row sense is the landscape sense.
branches.cn: 成排种植是景观义项。

branches.en: Fast growth and an upright shape make the tree easy to plant in lines.
branches.cn: 生长快、树形笔直，使杨树很适合成排栽种。

branches.en: Both crates and avenues come from the same pale, quick growing wood.
branches.cn: 木箱与林荫道都出自同一种浅色且速生的木材。

intro.en: Poplar is a whole Latin tree name borrowed into English, with no useful internal prefix or suffix to split off.
intro.cn: poplar 是一个整体借入英语的拉丁树名，内部没有可拆的有用前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin populus names the poplar tree, and the English compounds black poplar and white poplar simply add a colour word in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 populus 是杨树的名称，英语复合词 black poplar、white poplar 只是在前面加了颜色词。

items.meaning: a tall tree with trembling leaves
items.example: Poplar names the tree in modern English.
items.exampleCN: 现代英语用 poplar 指这种树。

items.example: The plural poplars names a line of trees.
items.exampleCN: 复数 poplars 指一整排树。

items.example: The compound black poplar adds a colour word.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 black poplar 前面加了颜色词。

items.meaning: a poplar with silvery leaf undersides
items.example: White poplar has leaves with pale undersides.
items.exampleCN: 银白杨的叶子背面发白。

items.example: Poplar wood is light and soft.
items.exampleCN: 杨木轻而软。

items.meaning: shaking, used inside the tree names quaking aspen and quaking poplar
items.meaningCN: 颤抖的，用于树名 quaking aspen、quaking poplar 中
items.example: The participle quaking describes the shivering leaves.
items.exampleCN: 分词 quaking 描写抖动的叶子。

items.meaning: not a suffix here, but the end of a borrowed tree name
items.meaningCN: 此处并非后缀，只是借入树名的结尾字母
